source.title: Cohomology of p-adic Stein spaces
source.authors: Pierre Colmez, Gabriel Dospinescu and Wiesława Nizioł
source.version: Authors’ manuscript dated 7 September 2019, 68 pages, at the recorded URL and SHA-256; independently read in full, including proofs and references. This is a public manuscript associated with the published article, not a verified copy of the version of record. arXiv:1801.06686v2 is dated 18 January 2019, 67 pages; its corresponding finding passages were collated, not the whole preprint reread. The arXiv history lists v1 and v2 at the review date. Springer supplies a subscription preview; journal pagination 873–985 was not independently checked. The manuscript date and matching appendix titles do not establish accepted-version identity.
readSections: Appendix A Alternative proof of Corollary 6.25

summary: The paper computes the p-adic étale and pro-étale cohomology of the Drinfeld symmetric space H^d_K = P^d_K minus its K-rational hyperplanes, and proves the comparison theorem for p-adic Stein spaces that the computation rests on. The answers (Theorem 1.3): H^r_ét(H^d_C,Q_p(r)) ≅ Sp^cont_r(Q_p)^*, the same dual of a Steinberg representation as in the ℓ-adic computation of Schneider–Stuhler, while H^r_proét(H^d_C,Q_p(r)) is a non-trivial extension of Sp_r(Q_p)^* by the huge Fréchet space Ω^{r−1}(H^d_C)/ker d; and étale cohomology is exactly the space of G-bounded vectors of pro-étale cohomology. The comparison theorem (Theorem 1.8) says that for a semistable Stein weak formal scheme X over O_K the pro-étale cohomology H^r_proét(X_C,Q_p(r)) is the pullback of (H^r_HK(X_k) ⊗̂_F B^+_st)^{N=0,φ=p^r} → H^r_dR(X_C) ← Ω^r(X_C)^{d=0}: a one-way comparison, built from Grosse-Klönne's overconvergent Hyodo–Kato cohomology and a piece of the de Rham complex, in contrast with the proper case, where the huge term disappears and an extra de Rham term appears. The route is syntomic: the Fontaine–Messing period map identifies syntomic with (pro-)étale cohomology after truncation; a Bloch–Kato style syntomic cohomology built from overconvergent differential forms is compared with it by Künneth maps that use the interpretation of period rings as crystalline cohomology of base rings, a rigidity of Frobenius eigenspaces and a change of topology available because a Stein space has proper smooth irreducible components in its special fibre. For the half-space the Hyodo–Kato term is computed by symbols, generalising Iovita–Spiess, and the étale side is computed integrally: the standard semistable model is pro-ordinary, its sheaves of differentials are acyclic with vanishing differential on global sections (Grosse-Klönne), so the syntomic cohomology reduces to the logarithmic de Rham–Witt cohomology H^0_ét(Ȳ,WΩ^r_log), which the mod p irreducibility of the Steinberg representation identifies with Sp^cont_r(Z_p)^*. All of this is carried out in the quasi-abelian category of locally convex Q_p-vector spaces and in pro-discrete O_K-modules, so that every isomorphism is topological and every sequence strictly exact.
conventions: Locators are the statement numbers of the authors’ manuscript (7 September 2019, 68 pages) together with its page numbers; the published pagination (Invent. Math. 219, 873–985) was not accessible. Numbering is by section with a single counter shared with the displayed equations, so gaps in the statement numbers (1.5, 2.4, 2.10–2.25, 3.3, 3.11, 3.14–3.15, …) are equations, not missing statements. K is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic 0 with perfect residue field k of characteristic p, O_K its ring of integers, ϖ a fixed uniformiser, e the ramification index of K over F, O_F = W(k), F = Frac O_F, C the p-adic completion of an algebraic closure K̄, and G_K = Gal(K̄/K); O_K, O^×_K, O^0_K are Spec or Spf of O_K with the trivial, canonical and (1 ↦ 0) log structures, and k^0 is the standard log point. For all Drinfeld-space and local-representation statements K/Q_p is finite (as required on pp. 2 and 37); the general Stein comparison allows the stated complete discretely valued K. G = GL_{d+1}(K) acts on the Drinfeld half-space H^d_K, whose standard semistable weak formal model is written H̃^d_K, with special fibre Y and Ȳ = Y_{k̄}. Square brackets [·] denote derived eigenspaces and round brackets the non-derived ones, and [C → C′] is the mapping fibre holim(C → C′ ← 0). H̃^i denotes cohomology in the left heart of the quasi-abelian category of convex spaces and H^i the algebraic cohomology with the subquotient topology; the two agree exactly when the cohomology is called classical. Sp_J, Sp^cont_J and Sp^an_J are the smooth, continuous and locally analytic generalized Steinberg representations, with Sp_r := Sp_{{1,…,d−r}}, and M^* is the weak topological dual. Unless stated otherwise formal schemes are p-adic, locally of finite type and equidimensional, and 'semistable' includes the log structure of the special fibre (self-intersections are allowed for weak formal schemes in §3.1 but excluded for formal schemes in §3.3). Keep Y=X_0 over k and Ȳ=Y_{k̄} distinct: integral WΩ on Y has W(k)=O_F coefficients, whereas the geometric base change has W(k̄) coefficients. Logarithmic Witt forms carry Z_p coefficients. Write RΓ_cr(Y/O_F^0,F) for sheafwise rational crystalline cohomology; it is not notation for RΓ_cr(Y/O_F^0)⊗Q_p on arbitrary non-quasi-compact Y.

items.name: The arithmetic setup and the three log structures on O_K
items.statement: O_K is a complete discrete valuation ring of mixed characteristic (0,p) with perfect residue field k and fraction field K; ϖ is a fixed uniformiser and e the ramification index of K over F; O_F = W(k) with fraction field F; K̄ is an algebraic closure of K, O_K̄ the integral closure of O_K in K̄, C = K̂̄ its p-adic completion and G_K = Gal(K̄/K); σ is the absolute Frobenius of W(k). The symbols O_K, O^×_K and O^0_K denote Spec(O_K) or Spf(O_K) with, respectively, the trivial log structure, the canonical log structure (associated with the closed point) and the log structure induced by N → O_K, 1 ↦ 0; likewise O^0_F denotes O_F with the log structure 1 ↦ 0. Unless stated otherwise all formal schemes are p-adic, locally of finite type and equidimensional; for X over O_K, X_0 is the special fibre and X_n the reduction modulo p^n.
items.note: CR.5 constructs prelog rings, log structures on the étale site, charts and the standard semistable chart, and says to carry the log structure along under reduction and completion; the three log structures on Spf O_K and the base O^0_F are exactly its objects. The paper is a consumer, not a source, here.

items.name: The period rings A_cr, B^+_cr, B^+_st, B^+_dR with φ, N, θ and the embedding ι_ϖ
items.statement: A_cr, B^+_cr, B^+_st, B^+_dR are Fontaine's crystalline, semistable and de Rham period rings. B^+_st = B^+_cr[u] with φ(u) = pu and N(u) = −1. The embedding ι = ι_ϖ : B^+_st → B^+_dR is defined by u ↦ u_ϖ = log([ϖ^♭]/ϖ), and the Galois action on B^+_st is the one induced from B^+_dR through this embedding. θ : B^+_st → C is Fontaine's projection (the composite of ι_ϖ with B^+_dR → C), and θ : A^{φ=p}_cr → O_C its integral avatar. A_cr,K and A_st denote the auxiliary period rings of §6.4 used for the integral (étale) computation.
items.note: CP.0 constructs "all ring maps to A_cris, B_cris, B_st and B_dR from the shared objects" and fixes the normalisation dictionary for θ, ξ, μ and Frobenius; R06.1 owns the period rings themselves. What this paper adds — the Künneth interpretation A_cr ≃ RΓ_cr(O_C) and the rigidity of φ-eigenspaces — is a separate item.

items.name: Working in the derived ∞-category of a quasi-abelian category, and the two-term homotopy limit bracket
items.statement: Unless otherwise stated one works in the derived (stable) ∞-category D(A) of left-bounded complexes of a quasi-abelian category A, and with (pre)sheaves of objects of D(A). For a map f : C → C′ in the derived ∞-category of a quasi-abelian category one writes [C —f→ C′] := holim(C → C′ ← 0), the homotopy fibre of f.
items.note: This bracket is the definition of every syntomic complex in the paper: RΓ_syn = [RΓ_cr^{φ=p^r} → RΓ_cr/F^r]. Nothing in the atlas builds quasi-abelian categories or their derived ∞-categories; see the §2 items.

items.name: The Drinfeld half-plane H_K = P^1_K ∖ P^1(K) and its GL_2(K)-action
items.statement: For [K : Q_p] < ∞, H_K := P^1_K ∖ P^1(K) is the Drinfeld half-plane, regarded as a rigid analytic space over K; it carries a natural action of G := GL_2(K) by homographies. One writes H_C := H_{K,C} for its base change to C.
items.note: ET.6a constructs Drinfeld towers for arbitrary n, including the n=2 half-plane here. Its existing scope is imported; the cohomology computations and standard-model comparison are separate contracts.

items.name: Fact 1.1 (Drinfeld): the ℓ-adic and p-adic étale cohomology of the half-plane is a Steinberg dual
items.statement: For every prime ℓ, including ℓ = p, there is a natural isomorphism of G × G_K-representations H^1_ét(H_C, Q_ℓ(1)) ≅ Sp^cont(Q_ℓ)^*, where Sp^cont(Q_ℓ) := C(P^1(K), Q_ℓ)/Q_ℓ is the continuous Steinberg representation of G with coefficients in Q_ℓ, with trivial G_K-action, and (−)^* is the weak topological dual.
items.note: The proof uses Kummer theory and the vanishing of the Picard groups of the standard Stein covering. Footnote 4, p. 4, records that "the proof of Drinfeld, in the case ℓ = p, is flawed but one can find a correct proof in [27]" (Fresnel–van der Put), as Grosse-Klönne and Berkovich pointed out to the authors; the companion paper PAPER-COLMEZ-DOSPINESCU-NIZIOL-20-B reports the same defect and supplies its own proof. This is the result that motivated the whole project, and Theorem 1.3 is its generalisation to all d and all r.

items.name: The Drinfeld half-space H^d_K = P^d_K ∖ ∪_{H ∈ H} H
items.statement: For d ≥ 1, H^d_K := P^d_K ∖ ∪_{H ∈ H} H, where H is the set of K-rational hyperplanes of P^d_K; it is a rigid analytic space over K carrying a natural action of G := GL_{d+1}(K). H^d_C denotes its base change to C. It is a Stein space, and it has a distinguished semistable formal model (the standard model of §5.1).
items.note: Nothing in the atlas has the Drinfeld half-space in dimension d > 1: ET.6a builds the towers of Lubin–Tate and Drinfeld type in the sense of p-divisible groups, and the ℓ-adic realisation, but not the symmetric space P^d ∖ hyperplanes with its Bruhat–Tits combinatorics.

items.name: The generalized locally constant and continuous Steinberg representations Sp_r and Sp^cont_r
items.statement: For 1 ≤ r ≤ d and a prime ℓ, Sp_r(Q_ℓ) and Sp^cont_r(Q_ℓ) denote the generalized locally constant and continuous Steinberg Q_ℓ-representations of G = GL_{d+1}(K) (constructed in §5.2.1), equipped with the trivial action of G_K. Their duals are what the cohomology of the half-space turns out to be.
items.note: The full construction, with the smooth, continuous and locally analytic variants and the duality and irreducibility statements, is in the §5 items.

items.name: Theorem 1.2 (Schneider–Stuhler): the ℓ-adic cohomology of the half-space, ℓ ≠ p
items.statement: Let r ≥ 0 and let ℓ ≠ p. There are natural G × G_K-equivariant isomorphisms H^r_ét(H^d_C, Q_ℓ(r)) ≅ Sp^cont_r(Q_ℓ)^* and H^r_proét(H^d_C, Q_ℓ(r)) ≅ Sp_r(Q_ℓ)^*.
items.note: Schneider–Stuhler's computation works for any cohomology theory satisfying certain axioms, the most important being homotopy invariance for the open unit ball — which "fails rather dramatically" for p-adic (pro-)étale cohomology, since the p-adic étale cohomology of the unit ball is huge. That is the difficulty the whole paper is built to circumvent.

items.name: Stein rigid analytic space
items.statement: A rigid analytic space Y is Stein if it has an admissible affinoid covering Y = ∪_{i ∈ N} U_i with U_i ⋐ U_{i+1}, i.e. the inclusion U_i ⊂ U_{i+1} factors over the adic compactification of U_i. The key property used is the acyclicity of the cohomology of coherent sheaves; in particular RΓ_dR(Y) ≅ Ω^•(Y) for Y Stein, and O(Y), Ω^i(Y) are Fréchet spaces.
items.note: The Drinfeld half-space and the rigid affine space are the examples. Nothing in the atlas builds Stein rigid spaces or their coherent acyclicity; the companion extraction PAPER-COLMEZ-DOSPINESCU-NIZIOL-20-B routed the curve case to the same missing package.

items.name: Bounded subsets and G-bounded vectors of a locally convex Q_p-vector space
items.statement: A subset X of a locally convex Q_p-vector space is bounded if p^n x_n → 0 for every sequence {x_n}, n ∈ N, of elements of X. A vector x is G-bounded if its G-orbit is a bounded set. (−)^{G-bd} denotes the subspace of G-bounded vectors.
items.note: Part (3) of Theorem 1.3 says that p-adic étale cohomology is exactly the G-bounded part of pro-étale cohomology; the same phenomenon is Theorem 0.5 of the companion paper.

items.name: Theorem 1.3: the p-adic étale and pro-étale cohomology of the Drinfeld half-space
items.statement: Let r ≥ 0. (1) There is a natural isomorphism of G × G_K-locally convex topological Q_p-vector spaces H^r_ét(H^d_C, Q_p(r)) ≅ Sp^cont_r(Q_p)^*, and these spaces are weak duals of Banach spaces. (2) There is a strictly exact sequence of G × G_K-Fréchet spaces 0 → Ω^{r−1}(H^d_C)/ker d → H^r_proét(H^d_C, Q_p(r)) → Sp_r(Q_p)^* → 0. (3) The natural map H^r_ét(H^d_C, Q_p(r)) → H^r_proét(H^d_C, Q_p(r)) identifies étale cohomology with the space of G-bounded vectors in pro-étale cohomology.
items.note: The main theorem. So the p-adic étale cohomology is the same Steinberg dual as its ℓ-adic counterpart, while the p-adic pro-étale cohomology is a non-trivial extension of that dual by a huge space. Part (3) is obtained only after parts (1) and (2); for a general rigid analytic variety the map from étale to pro-étale cohomology need not even be injective (the open unit ball over a field that is not spherically complete).

items.name: Remark 1.6: vanishing outside the range, and the finiteness properties of the two flanking spaces
items.statement: (i) For r ≥ d + 1 all the spaces of Theorem 1.3 are 0. (ii) For 1 ≤ r ≤ d the two outer spaces of the exact sequence of Theorem 1.3(2), despite being huge, are both duals of admissible locally analytic representations of G of finite length — over C on the left and over Q_p on the right; on the left this is due to Orlik–Strauch.
items.note: The locally analytic side (admissible locally analytic representations, Orlik–Strauch functors and their finite length) is the roadmap proposed by PAPER-DING-25; this paper is a consumer of it.

items.name: Remark 1.7: small Tate twists and the integral statement
items.statement: For small Tate twists (r ≤ p − 1) the Fontaine–Messing period map, an essential input in the proof of Theorem 1.3, is an isomorphism "on the nose"; with better control of the constants the proof would then give the integral statement H^r_ét(H^d_C, F_p(r)) ≅ Sp_r(F_p)^*. In fact, combining §6 of this paper with the integral p-adic Hodge theory of Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze and Česnavičius–Koshikawa, such a result holds for all twists; this is proved in the sequel [18].
items.note: Recorded as a gap: the integral statement is not proved here, and the sequel (PAPER-COLMEZ-DOSPINESCU-NIZIOL-21, "Integral p-adic étale cohomology of Drinfeld symmetric spaces", job #1322) is the paper that proves it. Independent review: The small-twist discussion is conditional on improving constants. The all-twist integral theorem and the étale regulator announced in Remark 6.46 belong to the sequel; they are not established here.

items.name: Theorem 1.8: the comparison theorem for p-adic pro-étale cohomology of a semistable Stein space
items.statement: Let r ≥ 0 and let X be a semistable Stein weak formal scheme over O_K. There is a commutative G_K-equivariant diagram of Fréchet spaces with strictly exact rows 0 → Ω^{r−1}(X_C)/ker d → H^r_proét(X_C, Q_p(r)) → (H^r_HK(X_k) ⊗̂_F B^+_st)^{N=0, φ=p^r} → 0 and 0 → Ω^{r−1}(X_C)/ker d —d→ Ω^r(X_C)^{d=0} —can→ H^r_dR(X_C) → 0, whose vertical maps are β̃ and ι_HK ⊗ θ. The maps β̃ and ι_HK ⊗ θ are strict and have closed images, and ker(β̃) ≅ ker(ι_HK ⊗ θ) ≅ (H^r_HK(X_k) ⊗̂_F B^+_st)^{N=0, φ=p^{r−1}}. Here H^r_HK(X_k) is Grosse-Klönne's overconvergent Hyodo–Kato cohomology, ι_HK : H^r_HK(X_k) ⊗_F K ≅ H^r_dR(X_K) is the Hyodo–Kato isomorphism, B^+_st is Fontaine's semistable period ring and θ : B^+_st → C his projection.
items.note: The main theorem of the paper, and the statement cited as "Theorem 1.8 of [17]" by the companion papers (it is what gives the closedness of the image in their fundamental diagram). CR.6 and CP.4 plan the Hyodo–Kato complex and the B_st comparison only for proper semistable models; this is the non-proper Stein case, in every dimension, and has no home in the atlas.

items.name: Example 1.9: the pro-étale cohomology of rigid affine space
items.statement: When the Hyodo–Kato cohomology vanishes, Theorem 1.8 gives a particularly simple formula. For the rigid affine space A^d_K and r ≥ 1 one has H^r_dR(A^d_K) = 0, hence H^r_HK(A^d_K) = 0 by the Hyodo–Kato isomorphism, and therefore H^r_proét(A^d_C, Q_p(r)) ≅ Ω^{r−1}(A^d_C)/ker d.
items.note: The authors say this was their first proof of the fact, and point to more direct arguments in [21] (Colmez–Nizioł) and in [52] (Le Bras).

items.name: Remark 1.10: the comparison is one-way, and what happens in the proper case
items.statement: (i) Theorem 1.8 is a one-way comparison theorem: H^r_proét(X_C, Q_p(r)) is the pullback of the diagram (H^r_HK(X_k) ⊗̂_F B^+_st)^{N=0, φ=p^r} —ι_HK⊗θ→ H^r_dR(X_K) ⊗̂_K C ←can— Ω^r(X_C)^{d=0}, built from Hyodo–Kato cohomology and a piece of the de Rham complex. (ii) If X is proper then Ω^{r−1}(X_K)/ker d = 0 (degeneration of the Hodge–de Rham spectral sequence) and the top row becomes 0 → H^r_proét(X_C,Q_p(r)) → (H^r_HK(X_k) ⊗̂_F B^+_st)^{N=0,φ=p^r} → (H^r_dR(X_K) ⊗̂_K B^+_dR)/Fil^r → 0: the huge term on the left disappears and an extra term appears on the right.
items.note: This is the conceptual content of the theorem: pro-étale cohomology is not determined by Hyodo–Kato cohomology alone, and the huge Fréchet term is exactly the failure of properness.

items.name: Proposition 1.11: the Fontaine–Messing period maps are strict quasi-isomorphisms after truncation
items.statement: Let X be a semistable Stein formal scheme over O_K. The Fontaine–Messing period morphisms α_FM : RΓ_syn(X_{O_C}, Q_p(r)) → RΓ_proét(X_C, Q_p(r)) and α_FM : RΓ_syn(X_{O_C}, Z_p(r))_{Q_p} → RΓ_ét(X_C, Q_p(r)) are strict quasi-isomorphisms after truncation τ^{≤r}.
items.note: The starting point of both computations: the classical comparison theorem between p-adic nearby cycles and syntomic sheaves (Tsuji, Colmez–Nizioł), specialised to Stein spaces. Proved as Proposition 6.1 for the étale case.

items.name: Fontaine–Messing (crystalline) geometric syntomic cohomology of a semistable formal scheme
items.statement: RΓ_syn(X_{O_C}, Z_p(r)) := [RΓ_cr(X_{O_C})^{φ=p^r} → RΓ_cr(X_{O_C})/F^r], where F^r RΓ_cr(X_{O_C}) := RΓ_cr(X_{O_C}, J^{[r]}), the crystalline cohomology is absolute (i.e. over W(k)), and [A → B] is the mapping fibre. RΓ_syn(X_{O_C}, Q_p(r)) is defined by taking RΓ_syn(−, Z_p(r))_{Q_p} on quasi-compact pieces and gluing.
items.note: PadicHodgeRegulators D.2 builds a syntomic mapping fibre with filtered de Rham complexes and Frobenius in the smooth unramified setting, for regulators; the semistable formal-scheme version over O_C, with the divided-power filtration J^{[r]} and the gluing over a Stein exhaustion, is not planned.

items.name: The Bloch–Kato syntomic cohomology route for the pro-étale topology, and the technical heart of the paper
items.statement: For the pro-étale topology one defines a Bloch–Kato syntomic cohomology RΓ^BK_syn(X_C, Q_p(r)) using overconvergent differential forms, which behaves well locally because of the imposed overconvergence, and constructs a map from Fontaine–Messing to Bloch–Kato syntomic cohomology, fitting in a commutative diagram of distinguished triangles RΓ_syn(X_{O_C},Q_p(r)) → RΓ_cr(X_{O_C},F)^{φ=p^r} → RΓ_cr(X_{O_C},F)/F^r above RΓ^BK_syn(X_C,Q_p(r)) → (RΓ_HK(X_k) ⊗̂_F B^+_st)^{N=0,φ=p^r} → (RΓ_dR(X_K) ⊗̂_K B^+_dR)/F^r above Ω^{≥r}(X_K) ⊗̂ C → Ω^•(X_K) ⊗̂_K C → Ω^{≤r−1}(X_K) ⊗̂_K C, in which the top vertical maps are isomorphisms. These maps are Künneth maps using the interpretation of period rings as crystalline cohomology of certain base rings (for example A_cr ≃ RΓ_cr(O_C)), coupled with a rigidity of the φ-eigenspaces of crystalline cohomology, followed by a change of topology from crystalline to overconvergent, which is possible because X_K is Stein and hence X_k has proper smooth irreducible components. The bottom vertical maps are induced by θ : B^+_dR → C and use RΓ_dR(X_K) ≃ Ω^•(X_K) for X Stein. Theorem 1.8 follows by applying H^r.
items.note: The authors call the construction of the top vertical maps and the proof that they are isomorphisms "the technical heart of this paper"; it is §§3–4. To control topologies they work in the derived category of locally convex Q_p-vector spaces, which is reasonable because Q_p is spherically complete.

items.name: The Hyodo–Kato cohomology of the half-space is a Steinberg dual, and (1.12)
items.statement: For X the standard model of H^d_K one has (H^r_HK(X_k) ⊗̂_F B^+_st)^{N=0, φ=p^r} ≅ Sp_r(Q_p)^*  (1.12). This follows from H^r_HK(X_k) ≅ Sp_r(F)^*, an isomorphism which is unique once required to be compatible with the standard symbols, and which is obtained from Schneider–Stuhler's H^r_dR(X_K) ≅ Sp_r(K)^*, the fact that both sides are generated by standard symbols — cup products of symbols of K-rational hyperplanes viewed as invertible functions on X_K (for the de Rham side this is Iovita–Spiess, and the isomorphism is compatible with symbols) — the Hyodo–Kato isomorphism and the irreducibility of Sp_r(K)^*. It yields H^r_HK(X_k)^{φ=p^r} ≅ Sp_r(Q_p)^* and H^r_HK(X_k) ≅ F ⊗_{Q_p} H^r_HK(X_k)^{φ=p^r}.
items.note: This is how the abstract comparison theorem is turned into the concrete answer: the pro-étale part of Theorem 1.3 is Theorem 1.8 plus (1.12). The symbol argument is the reason §7 exists.

items.name: The integral route for étale cohomology: γ_HK, the complex HK_r and the identifications (1.13)–(1.15)
items.statement: For the étale topology one obtains instead a strict quasi-isomorphism of distinguished triangles identifying RΓ_syn(X_{O_C},Z_p(r))_{Q_p} → RΓ_cr(X_{O_C})^{φ=p^r}_{Q_p} → RΓ_cr(X_{O_C})_{Q_p}/F^r with RΓ_syn(X_{O_C},Z_p(r))_{Q_p} → (RΓ_cr(X_k/O^0_F) ⊗̂_{O_F} Â_st)^{N=0,φ=p^r}_{Q_p} —γ_HK ⊗ ι→ (RΓ_dR(X) ⊗̂_{O_K} A_cr,K)/F^r, where O^0_F is O_F with the log structure 1 ↦ 0. In general γ_HK is hard to identify; for the standard model X of H^d_K, writing HK_r := (RΓ_cr(X_k/O^0_F) ⊗̂_{O_F} Â_st)^{N=0,φ=p^r}_{Q_p}, the acyclicity of the sheaves of differentials (Grosse-Klönne) gives G × G_K-equivariant strict (quasi-)isomorphisms H^r HK_r ≅ H^0_ét(X_{k̄}, WΩ^r_log)_{Q_p} and H^{r−1} HK_r ≅ (H^0_ét(X_{k̄}, WΩ^{r−1}_log) ⊗̂_{Z_p} A^{φ=p}_cr)_{Q_p}, and (RΓ_dR(X) ⊗̂_{O_K} A_cr,K)/F^r ≅ ⊕_{r−1 ≥ i ≥ 0} (H^0(X, Ω^i) ⊗̂_{O_K} A_cr,K)/F^{r−i}[−i]  (1.13). These rest on H^0_ét(X_{k̄}, WΩ^r_log) ⊗̂_{Z_p} W(k̄) ≅ H^r_cr(X_{k̄}/W(k̄)^0) and on the integral Hyodo–Kato isomorphism ι_HK : H^r_cr(X_k/O^0_F) ⊗_{O_F} K ≅ H^r_dR(X) ⊗_{O_K} K  (1.14). One then gets the long exact sequence (H^0_ét(X_{k̄},WΩ^{r−1}_log) ⊗̂_{Z_p} A^{φ=p}_cr)_{Q_p} —γ′_HK→ (H^0(X,Ω^{r−1}) ⊗̂_{O_K} O_C)_{Q_p} → H^r_syn(X_{O_C},Z_p(r))_{Q_p} → H^0_ét(X_{k̄}, WΩ^r_log)_{Q_p} → 0, checks that γ′_HK is surjective — the Hyodo–Kato isomorphism holds already integrally and γ′_HK = ι_HK ⊗ θ with θ : A^{φ=p}_cr → O_C — and concludes H^r_syn(X_{O_C},Z_p(r))_{Q_p} ≅ H^0_ét(X_{k̄},WΩ^r_log)_{Q_p}, topologically. It remains to prove H^0_ét(X_{k̄}, WΩ^r_log)_{Q_p} ≅ Sp^cont_r(Q_p)^*  (1.15).
items.note: The surjectivity of γ′_HK is called "a bit surprising"; it is Corollary 6.42. The pro-ordinarity of X_k (Corollary 6.18) is what makes the de Rham–Witt computation work, and morally follows from X_k being a normal crossing scheme whose closed strata are products of blow-ups of projective spaces, hence classically ordinary. Independent review: In (1.13)–(1.15), logarithmic forms and the W(k̄) comparison use the geometric special fibre X_{k̄}; the integral crystalline input before base change is X_k. The hat on Â_st and all derived eigenspace brackets must be retained. See the corrected detailed item 6-lemma-6-37.

items.name: The proof of (1.15) and of part (3): passing to k̄ and comparing G-bounded vectors
items.statement: The isomorphism (1.15) is proved (Theorem 6.45) by replacing k with k̄ and using H^0_ét(X_k̄, WΩ^r_log) ⊗_{Z_p} K —f→ H^r_dR(X_K)^{G-bd} ≅ (Sp_r(K)^*)^{G-bd} ←≅— Sp^cont_r(Q_p)^* ⊗_{Q_p} K, where the second isomorphism is Schneider–Stuhler's. The map f, a composite of natural maps with the Hyodo–Kato isomorphism, is injective by pro-ordinarity of Y, and surjective because H^0_ét(X_k̄, WΩ^r_log) is compact and non-trivial while Sp^cont_r(Z_p)/p ≅ Sp_r(F_p) is irreducible — a non-trivial fact proved by Grosse-Klönne. Part (3) of Theorem 1.3 then follows from parts (1) and (2), their compatibility, and the identifications (Sp_r(K)^*)^{G-bd} ≅ Sp^cont_r(Q_p)^* ⊗_{Q_p} K and H^r_dR(X_K)^{G-bd} ≅ H^r_dR(X) ⊗_{O_K} K, the latter using that X can be covered by G-translates of an open subscheme U with U_K affinoid.
items.note: The mod p irreducibility of the continuous Steinberg representation is the pivotal input; it is Grosse-Klönne [37, Cor. 4.3].

items.name: Locally convex K-vector spaces and the quasi-abelian category C_K
items.statement: A K-topological vector space is a K-vector space with a linear topology; it is locally convex (convex) if there is a neighbourhood basis of the origin consisting of O_K-submodules. C_K is the category of convex K-vector spaces, not assumed separated, with continuous K-linear maps; it is quasi-abelian (Prosmans 2.1.11). Kernels, cokernels, images and coimages are computed in K-vector spaces and given the induced topology: ker and im with the subspace topology, coker and coim with the quotient topology. Since K is spherically complete the theory resembles the archimedean one. Two elementary observations are used constantly: if F is separated and f : E → F is injective then E is separated; and if in addition F is finite dimensional and f is bijective then f is an isomorphism in C_K.
items.note: An additive category with kernels and cokernels is quasi-abelian if every pullback of a strict epimorphism is a strict epimorphism and every pushout of a strict monomorphism is a strict monomorphism — equivalently, if Ext(−,−) is bifunctorial. Neither Mathlib nor Tau Ceti has quasi-abelian categories (only abelian ones), and neither has locally convex vector spaces over a nonarchimedean field: Mathlib's LocallyConvexSpace is the archimedean (ordered-field, convex-set) notion.

items.name: Strict morphisms, strict complexes, strictly exact sequences and strict quasi-isomorphisms
items.statement: A morphism f : E → F in C_K is strict if and only if it is relatively open: for every neighbourhood V of 0 in E there is a neighbourhood V′ of 0 in F with f(V) ⊇ V′ ∩ f(E); equivalently the natural map coim(f) → im(f) is an isomorphism. C_K carries the exact structure whose admissible monomorphisms are the embeddings and whose admissible epimorphisms are the open surjections. A complex is strict if all its differentials are; a sequence A —e→ B —f→ C with f∘e = 0 is strictly exact if e is strict and im(e) → ker(f) is an isomorphism; a complex is strictly acyclic if it is strictly exact in every degree; and a morphism of complexes whose cone is strictly exact is a strict quasi-isomorphism.
items.note: Mathlib has the notion itself: Topology.IsStrictMap (Mathlib/Topology/Maps/Strict/Basic.lean, "open onto its image") with IsStrictMap.continuous and the characterisations LinearMap.isStrictMap_iff_isOpenQuotientMap_rangeRestrict and LinearMap.isStrictMap_iff_isHomeomorph_quotKerEquivRange used by Tau Ceti. What is missing is the exact structure on a category of convex spaces built from it, and strict exactness of complexes. Independent review: The named strict-map carrier and its linear characterizations exist; the exact category, strict complexes and strict quasi-isomorphisms in this item do not follow just from that carrier.
items.statusReview: The named strict-map carrier and its linear characterizations exist; the exact category, strict complexes and strict quasi-isomorphisms in this item do not follow just from that carrier.

items.name: The open mapping theorem and the closed-range criterion for strictness, in the complete metrisable case
items.statement: A continuous surjection between Fréchet spaces (in particular between Banach spaces) is open, hence strict. Consequently, for E, F Fréchet, a morphism f : E → F is strict if and only if f(E) is closed in F: the "if" is the open mapping theorem applied to E → f(E), and the "only if" holds because a Fréchet space is metric and a complete subspace of a metric space is closed.
items.note: Tau Ceti proves exactly this over a Tate ring: TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.isOpenMap (TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber/OpenMapping.lean) for a surjective A-linear map, continuous at 0, from a complete nonarchimedean A-module with countably generated uniformity onto a complete T0 one, and TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.isStrictMap_of_isClosed_range for the closed-range criterion, with TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.isQuotientMap for the quotient form. K-Fréchet spaces are complete with countably generated uniformity, so these are the statements the paper uses; only the LF case below is beyond them. Independent review: Tau Ceti supplies the open-map and closed-range-to-strict implications with the binders checked below. The full Fréchet categorical statement still needs the nonarchimedean carrier/instance bridge and the quotient-completeness proof for the converse; retain those as proof tasks rather than claiming the entire bundle is a declaration.
items.statusReview: Tau Ceti supplies the open-map and closed-range-to-strict implications with the binders checked below. The full Fréchet categorical statement still needs the nonarchimedean carrier/instance bridge and the quotient-completeness proof for the converse; retain those as proof tasks rather than claiming the entire bundle is a declaration.

items.name: The open mapping theorem for LF-spaces
items.statement: An LF-space is a countable inductive limit of Fréchet spaces (LB if the terms are Banach). If f : X → Y is a continuous surjection of locally convex K-vector spaces and both X and Y are LF-spaces, then f is open.
items.note: This is the version the paper needs when it works with the LB/LF spaces Ω^i(X_K), Sp_J(Λ) and ker d^i ⊗̂ B^+_dR/F^j; an LF-space is not metrisable, so the Tau Ceti Tate-ring theorem (countably generated uniformity) does not cover it.

items.name: Truncations, the cohomology objects H̃^n, the left heart LH(C_K) and the notion of classical cohomology
items.statement: For E ∈ C(C_K) set τ^{≤n}E := (… → E^{n−1} → ker d^n → 0 → …) and τ^{≥n}E := (… → 0 → coim d^{n−1} → E^n → …), and H̃^n(E) := τ^{≤n}τ^{≥n}E = (coim d^{n−1} → ker d^n); cohomology taken in K-vector spaces, with the subquotient topology, is called algebraic and written H^n. D(C_K) is the left-bounded derived ∞-category; D^{≤n}(C_K) and D^{≥n}(C_K), the complexes strictly exact in degrees > n resp. < n, form a t-structure (Schneiders) whose left heart LH(C_K) is abelian: each of its objects is represented by a monomorphism f : E → F with F in degree 0, and by coker f when f is strict. The embedding I : C_K ↪ LH(C_K), E ↦ (0 → E), induces an equivalence D(C_K) ≅ D(LH(C_K)) compatible with the t-structures, the classical-part functor C : LH(C_K) → C_K sends f to coker f, C∘I ≅ Id and there is a natural epimorphism Id → I∘C. The cohomological functors H̃^n satisfy C∘H̃^n = H^n and come with a natural epimorphism H̃^n → I∘H^n; when this is an isomorphism on a given object, one says its cohomology is classical, i.e. the quotient topology on coim d^{n−1} agrees with the topology induced from ker d^n. Two facts are used repeatedly: an extension in LH(C_K) of objects in the image of I is in the image of I; and a complex of C_K is strictly exact in a degree if and only if D(I)(E) is exact there. There is a dual (right) version with costrict morphisms, the right abelian envelope RH(C_K) and H̃^n = (coker d^{n−1} → im d^n).
items.note: "Classical" is the property asserted of the syntomic and étale cohomology groups in Lemmas 3.26, 3.28 and Corollaries 6.42, 6.44 — it is what makes the topological statements of Theorems 1.3 and 1.8 meaningful. Mathlib has derived categories of abelian categories (DerivedCategory) but no quasi-abelian t-structure theory and no left/right hearts.

items.name: Lemma 2.1: algebraic acyclicity implies strict acyclicity for Banach or Fréchet complexes
items.statement: (1) If E is a complex of Banach spaces, or a complex of Fréchet spaces, with trivial algebraic cohomology, then E is strictly acyclic. (2) A morphism of complexes of Banach or of Fréchet spaces which is an algebraic quasi-isomorphism is a strict quasi-isomorphism.
items.note: Proved from the closed-range criterion: the kernel of a differential is closed, hence Fréchet, and algebraic exactness makes each image a closed subspace. The authors say they spell it out "because we will use it all the time"; it is invoked for instance in Corollary 3.46, where the period map is locally a zigzag of complexes of Banach spaces.

items.name: The projective and injective tensor topologies, their coincidence over a spherically complete field, and ⊗̂_K
items.statement: For V, W ∈ C_K the tensor product V ⊗_K W carries the projective topology V ⊗_{K,π} W (universal for jointly continuous bilinear maps) and the injective topology V ⊗_{K,ε} W (defined by cross seminorms with a product formula, the weakest such); V ⊗̂_{K,α} W denotes the Hausdorff completion for α = π, ε. The functor (−) ⊗_{K,π} W preserves strict epimorphisms and (−) ⊗_{K,ε} W preserves strict monomorphisms, and the natural map V ⊗_{K,π} W → V ⊗_{K,ε} W is an isomorphism because K is spherically complete, so one writes V ⊗_K W and V ⊗̂_K W. Consequently (−) ⊗̂_K W is left exact: it carries a strictly exact sequence 0 → V_1 → V_2 → V_3 → 0 to a strictly exact 0 → V_1 ⊗̂ W → V_2 ⊗̂ W → V_3 ⊗̂ W, the image of the last map is dense, and that map is surjective when its image is complete — for instance when all the V_i and W are Fréchet.
items.note: The completed tensor product is the basic operation of the whole paper (RΓ_HK ⊗̂_F B^+_st, Ω^i(X_K) ⊗̂_K B^+_dR, H^0_ét(Y,WΩ^r_log) ⊗̂_{Z_p} A^{φ=p}_cr). Nothing in the libraries has nonarchimedean projective/injective tensor topologies; Mathlib has algebraic tensor products and completions of uniform spaces only.

items.name: Commutation of the completed tensor product with countable projective limits and with regular nuclear inductive limits
items.statement: For V = lim←_n V_n with each V_n Fréchet and W Fréchet, the natural map V ⊗̂_{K,π} W → lim←_n (V_n ⊗̂_{K,π} W) is an isomorphism. For {V_n} a regular inductive system of Fréchet spaces with injective nuclear transition maps and W a Banach space, lim→_n (V_n ⊗̂_K W) → (lim→_n V_n) ⊗̂_K W is an isomorphism. Here an inductive system with injective transition maps is regular if every bounded set of V = lim→_n V_n is contained in and bounded in some V_n, and a map f : V → W is nuclear if it factors as V → V_1 —f_1→ W_1 → W with f_1 a compact map of Banach spaces.
items.note: These two interchanges are what make the explicit computations of §§3–4 possible (they are cited at pp. 21, 23 and 24). Nuclearity and compactness of maps of nonarchimedean Banach spaces (compactoid images) are not in the libraries.

items.name: Acyclic inductive systems and Wengenroth's criterion (Proposition 2.2)
items.statement: An inductive system {V_n}, n ∈ N, of locally convex K-vector spaces is acyclic if L^1hocolim_n V_n = 0. Proposition 2.2: an inductive system of Fréchet spaces with injective transition maps is acyclic if and only if in every V_n there is a convex neighbourhood U_n of 0 such that U_n ⊆ U_{n+1} for all n, and for every n there is m > n such that all the topologies of the V_k with k > m coincide on U_n.
items.note: This is the criterion that lets an inductive limit of Banach spaces be treated as exact, used for the spaces of compact type Ω^i(X_K) at pp. 23–24 and in Lemma 2.3(2).

items.name: The derived completed tensor product ⊗̂^R_K and Lemma 2.3: when it agrees with ⊗̂_K
items.statement: C_K has enough injectives, so the left exact functor (−) ⊗̂_K (−) has a right derived functor V ⊗̂^R_K W, computed from an injective resolution W → I^• as V ⊗̂_K I^•. The natural map V ⊗̂_K W → V ⊗̂^R_K W is a strict quasi-isomorphism when (1) V and W are both Fréchet, or (2) V = lim→_n V_n for an acyclic inductive system {V_n} of Banach spaces and W is a Banach space. The proof takes an injective resolution of W by Fréchet (resp. Banach) spaces — these exist by Prosmans 2.1.12 — and checks that the resulting sequence 0 → V ⊗̂ W → V ⊗̂ I^0 → V ⊗̂ I^1 → … is strictly exact.
items.note: Used at pp. 21 and 23 to replace ⊗̂^R by ⊗̂ in the Hyodo–Kato and de Rham terms, which is what makes the fundamental diagram a diagram of honest Fréchet spaces. In case (2) the proof interchanges ⊗̂ with the inductive limit, citing §2.1.3, whose point (5) requires a regular system with injective nuclear transition maps; recorded in sourceIssues.

items.name: The category PD_K of pro-discrete O_K-modules, the pseudocompact subcategory PC_K, and Ind(PD_K)
items.statement: PD_K is the category of topological O_K-modules that are countable inverse limits, as topological O_K-modules, of discrete O_K-modules, with continuous O_K-linear maps; it is quasi-abelian, has countable filtered projective limits, and countable products in it are exact. Its objects need not be separated for the p-adic topology: a Banach space B with unit ball B_0 is the object lim←_n B/p^n B_0, so Banach spaces and countable products or projective limits of Banach spaces (Fréchet spaces) are objects of PD_K. Inside PD_K, PC_K is the abelian category of pseudocompact modules, i.e. M ≅ lim←_i M_i with each M_i of finite length (equivalently profinite when [K:Q_p] < ∞); it has exact countable products and exact countable filtered projective limits. Ind(PD_K) is the ind-completion: it is quasi-abelian, PD_K → Ind(PD_K) is exact, it has filtered inductive limits and projective limits, lim← is left exact on it, and a functor out of PD_K is left (right) exact if and only if its extension is.
items.note: This is the integral category in which all the étale computations of §6 live ("in every degree we have a product of Z_p-modules with p-adic topology"). Nothing in the libraries has pro-discrete or pseudocompact modules as a category, although Mathlib has profinite sets and adic completions.

items.name: The completed tensor product of pro-discrete modules and its exactness
items.statement: For M, N ∈ PD_K, M ⊗̂_{O_K} N := lim←_{U ∈ U_M, V ∈ U_N} M/U ⊗_{O_K} N/V, where U_M, U_N are the inductive systems of open submodules and each M/U ⊗_{O_K} N/V is discrete; it is a pro-discrete O_K-module with the expected universal property. In general it is neither left nor right exact; it is right exact on PC_K, and it commutes with filtered limits N = lim←_i N_i for which N surjects onto every N_i — in particular with products of pro-discrete modules and with filtered limits of pseudocompact modules.
items.note: Used for the integral period computations of §6, e.g. H^0_ét(Y,WΩ^{r−1}_log) ⊗̂_{Z_p} A^{φ=p}_cr. "Right exact" means here: carries strict exact sequences to costrict exact sequences (Schneiders' functor RR).

items.name: The functor (−) ⊗ K from pro-discrete modules to convex spaces, and its derived functors
items.statement: Since K ≅ lim→(O_K —ϖ→ O_K —ϖ→ …), for M ∈ PD_K the module M ⊗_{O_K} K = lim→(M —ϖ→ M —ϖ→ …) carries the inductive limit topology, giving a functor (−) ⊗ K : PD_K → C_K, extended to Ind(PD_K) because C_K has filtered inductive limits. It must not be confused with the completed tensor product (−) ⊗̂ K : PD_K → PD_K, which is always zero. The functor (−) ⊗ K is right exact but not in general left exact: tensoring the strict exact sequence 0 → ∏_{i≥0} p^i Z_p → ∏_{i≥0} Z_p → ∏_{i≥0} Z_p/p^i → 0 with Q_p is not costrict exact on the left, and (∏_{i≥0} Z_p/p^i) ⊗ Q_p is not Hausdorff. One therefore uses the left derived functors (−) ⊗^L K : D^-(PD_K) → Pro(D^-(C_K)) and (−) ⊗^L K : D^-(Ind(PD_K)) → Pro(D^-(C_K)), the target being a pro-category.
items.note: This is the functor that turns the integral (pro-discrete) complexes of §6 into the locally convex Q_p-complexes in which the main theorems are stated; the counterexample is the reason the rationalisation has to be derived.

items.name: Proposition 2.6 and Lemma 2.7: rationalisation is undistorted on torsion-free p-adically complete complexes
items.statement: Proposition 2.6: if E is a complex of torsion-free, p-adically complete (E ≅ lim←_n E/p^n) modules of PD_K, then the natural map E ⊗^L K → E ⊗ K is a strict quasi-isomorphism. Lemma 2.7: if 0 → A → B —π→ C → 0 is a strict exact sequence of pro-discrete O_K-modules and C is torsion-free and p-adically complete, then π admits a continuous O_K-linear section and B ≅ A ⊕ C as a topological O_K-module. Lemma 2.7 says the terms of E are acyclic for (−) ⊗ K, which gives Proposition 2.6.
items.note: Used at pp. 44 and 56 to commute the rationalisation with truncation and with the period maps. The proof of Lemma 2.7 builds the section by hand: write the sequence as a limit of exact sequences of discrete modules, choose Teichmüller-style liftings of a k-basis of the graded pieces of C/ϖ, and assemble a topological isomorphism from ∏_i ℓ^0_∞(J_i, O_K) onto C by a convergent double series; the index set of the elements of that product is misprinted (recorded in sourceIssues).

items.name: Overconvergent Tate algebras, dagger algebras and dagger spaces
items.statement: For K = K or C and δ ∈ R_+, T_n(δ) := K{δ^{-1}X_1,…,δ^{-1}X_n} = {Σ_v a_v X^v : |a_v|δ^{|v|} → 0}; for δ ∈ p^Q it is an affinoid K-algebra with the norm max_v |a_v|δ^{|v|}. K[X_1,…,X_n]^† := ∪_{δ>1, δ∈p^Q} T_n(δ), a Hausdorff LF-space. A dagger algebra is a topological K-algebra isomorphic to a quotient of some K[X_1,…,X_n]^†; it is a Hausdorff LF-algebra and defines a sheaf O^† of topological K-algebras on Sp(Â) (a dagger structure). A dagger affinoid is Sp(A) := (|Sp Â|, O^†). A dagger space is a pair (X̂, O^†) with X̂ a rigid analytic space over K and O^† a sheaf of topological K-algebras which is locally a dagger structure; Γ(X,O^†) carries the convex structure lim←_Y Γ(Y,O^†|_Y) over affinoid subsets Y.
items.note: Nothing in the libraries or the atlas has overconvergent (dagger) spaces: Tau Ceti builds Huber pairs, Tate rings and adic spaces (TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber/*), but not weak completions or overconvergent structure sheaves.

items.name: U ⋐_Y X, partially proper and proper dagger spaces, and the equivalence with rigid spaces
items.statement: For a morphism X = Sp(A) → Y = Sp(B) of affinoid dagger spaces and an affinoid subdomain U ⊆ X, write U ⋐_Y X if there are a surjection τ : B[X_1,…,X_r]^† → A and δ ∈ p^Q, δ > 1, with U ⊆ Sp(A[δ^{-1}τ(X_1),…,δ^{-1}τ(X_r)]^†). A morphism f : X → Y of dagger (or rigid) spaces is partially proper if it is separated and there are admissible coverings Y = ∪Y_i, f^{-1}(Y_i) = ∪X_{ij} such that each X_{ij} satisfies X_{ij} ⋐_Y X̃_{ij} for some affinoid X̃_{ij} ⊆ f^{-1}(Y_i); a quasi-compact partially proper dagger space is proper, compatibly with the rigid notion. The category of partially proper dagger spaces is equivalent to the category of partially proper rigid spaces (Grosse-Klönne); in particular the rigid analytification of a finite type K-scheme is partially proper, and Stein spaces are partially proper.
items.note: This equivalence is what lets the paper pass between the dagger world, where overconvergent cohomology is defined, and the rigid world, where the étale and pro-étale cohomology of the main theorems live; it is used again as ι²_rig in Theorem 4.1.

items.name: Stein dagger spaces, Stein coverings, and weak formal schemes
items.statement: A dagger (or rigid) space X is Stein if it has an admissible affinoid covering X = ∪_{i∈N} U_i with U_i ⊂^† U_{i+1}, meaning that Û_i = Sp(C) ⊂ Û_{i+1} = Sp(D) is induced by a map D ≅ T_n(δ)/I → C ≅ T_n/I T_n with δ > 1; such a covering is a Stein covering. A weakly complete O_K-algebra A^† is a ϖ-adically separated O_K-algebra in which every series f(x_1,…,x_n) converges, for f = Σ a_v X^v ∈ O_K{X_1,…,X_n} satisfying c(v_p(a_v)+1) ≥ |v| for some constant c and all v; the weak completion of A is the smallest weakly complete subalgebra of Â containing the image of A. An affine weak formal scheme is Spwf(A^†) = (Spec(A^†/ϖ), O) with Γ(X_f,O) = (A^†_f)^† for a weakly complete finitely generated A^†; a weak formal scheme is locally of this form. For X flat over O_K, the dagger space X_K is partially proper if and only if every irreducible closed subset of X is proper over O_K.
items.note: Weak formal schemes are the objects on which overconvergent syntomic cohomology is defined, and the "Stein" hypothesis is what all the comparison theorems need. Neither library has weak formal schemes.

items.name: Semistable and Stein (weak) formal schemes; Stein with semistable reduction and the ideally log-smooth truncations
items.statement: A weak formal scheme over O_K is semistable if locally for the Zariski topology it admits étale maps to Spwf(O_K[X_1,…,X_n]^†/(X_1⋯X_r − ϖ)), 1 ≤ r ≤ n, and it carries the log structure of the special fibre; the same definition is made for p-adic formal schemes (self-intersections are allowed here, but excluded in §3.3.1). A (weak) formal scheme is Stein if its generic fibre is Stein. X is Stein with a semistable reduction if it is Stein and semistable (in this partially proper setting the irreducible components of Y = X_0 are proper and smooth) and there are closed subschemes Y_s and open subschemes U_s of Y, s ∈ N, with: each Y_s a finite union of irreducible components; Y_s ⊆ U_s ⊆ Y_{s+1} with union Y; and the tubes {]U_s[_X} a Stein covering of X_K. The Y_s are not log-smooth over k^0 but are ideally log-smooth: an idealized log-scheme is a log-scheme together with an ideal of its log structure mapping to zero in the structure sheaf, and log-crystalline, log-convergent, log-rigid cohomology and de Rham–Witt complexes all extend to them.
items.note: The exhaustion {U_s},{Y_s} is used in every limit argument of the paper (Theorem 4.1, (7.5), Proposition 6.23). CR.5 plans log structures and log-smoothness but not idealized log-schemes.

items.name: Overconvergent log-rigid cohomology RΓ_rig(Y/O^0_F) built by hand from embedding systems
items.statement: Since the foundations of log-rigid cohomology are missing, RΓ_rig(Y/O^0_F) is constructed directly, following Grosse-Klönne. For Y a fine k^0-log-scheme choose an open covering Y = ∪_{i∈I} Y_i and exact closed immersions Y_i ↪ Z_i into log-smooth weak formal O^0_F-log-schemes; for every finite ∅ ≠ J ⊆ I choose an exactification Y_J = ∩_{i∈J} Y_i ↪ Z_J → ∏_{O^0_F}(Z_i)_{i∈J} of the diagonal embedding (Kato, Prop. 4.10). The tube ]Y_J[_{Z_J} with the restricted de Rham complex Ω^•_{]Y_J[_{Z_J}} := Ω^•_{Z_J,F}|_{]Y_J[_{Z_J}} depends only on the embedding system, not on the exactification, and Γ(]Y_J[_{Z_J},Ω^•) carries the topology of the dagger space. Well-ordering I gives a simplicial dagger space ]Y_•[_{Z_•}, and one sets RΓ_rig(Y/O^0_F) := hocolim Γ(]Y_•[_{Z_•},Ω^•) ∈ D(C_F), the colimit over the (homotopy-filtered) category of hypercovers built from such data, the affine ones being cofinal. The same construction over O^×_K gives RΓ_rig(Y/O^×_K) ∈ D(C_K).
items.note: PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology RD.4 plans rigid cohomology, but not the logarithmic and overconvergent version for semistable log-schemes over the log point, which is what Hyodo–Kato cohomology is here. Note that the printed statement places RΓ_rig(M_•/O^0_F) in D(C_K) rather than D(C_F); recorded in sourceIssues.

items.name: Frobenius and monodromy on overconvergent rigid cohomology, and the relation Nφ = pφN
items.statement: RΓ_rig(Y/O^0_F) carries a Frobenius endomorphism φ obtained by lifting Frobenius to the weak formal schemes Z_i. If Y is log-smooth over k^0 there is in addition a monodromy endomorphism N = Res(∇(dlog 0)) defined by the logarithmic connection, and pφN = Nφ (the formal definition of N is Nekovář–Nizioł, formula (37)). On the base r^† the Frobenius is T ↦ T^p and the monodromy is N = Res(∇(dlog T)); the specialisation p_0 : RΓ_rig(X/r^†) → RΓ_rig(X/O^0_F) induced by T ↦ 0 is compatible with both.
items.note: CR.6 constructs Frobenius and monodromy on the Hyodo–Kato complex of a proper semistable model with the relation Nφ = pφN in a chosen convention; the paper needs the same structures on the overconvergent, non-proper version, so CR.6 is a source for the conventions and this paper is a source for the overconvergent case. Independent review: CR.6 covers proper semistable Hyodo–Kato complexes. The overconvergent log-rigid construction and nonproper scope here need an extension.
items.statusReview: CR.6 covers proper semistable Hyodo–Kato complexes. The overconvergent log-rigid construction and nonproper scope here need an extension.

items.name: Proposition 3.2: finiteness, canonical topology and mixedness of overconvergent Hyodo–Kato cohomology
items.statement: Let Y be a semistable scheme over k with the induced log structure. (1) If Y is quasi-compact then H^*_rig(Y/O^0_F) is a finite dimensional F-vector space with its unique locally convex Hausdorff topology. (2) φ is a homeomorphism on H^*_rig(Y/O^0_F). (3) If k is finite then H^*_rig(Y/O^0_F) is a mixed F-isocrystal: the eigenvalues of the linearised Frobenius φ^f, |k| = p^f, are Weil numbers. The proof uses the weight spectral sequence E_1^{−k,i+k} = ⊕_{j ≥ 0, j ≥ −k} ∏_{S ∈ Θ_{2j+k+1}} H^{i−2j−k}_rig(S/O_F) ⇒ H^i_rig(Y/O^0_F), where Θ_j is the set of intersections of j distinct irreducible components of Y with trivial log structure, all smooth over k.
items.note: The weight spectral sequence is also what bounds the Frobenius slopes by the degree, which is the hypothesis of Lemma 3.39 and hence what makes the fundamental diagram exact.

items.name: Lemma 3.4 and Remark 3.5: the de Rham differentials of a smooth Stein or affinoid dagger space are strict with closed image
items.statement: If X is a smooth Stein space or a smooth affinoid dagger space then all de Rham differentials d^i : Ω^i(X) → Ω^{i+1}(X) are strict and have closed images. The same holds for log-smooth Stein spaces whose log structure comes from a normal crossing divisor, because for such quasi-compact log-smooth spaces the rigid de Rham cohomology agrees with that of the locus where the log structure is trivial, hence is finite dimensional with its canonical Hausdorff topology.
items.locator: Lemma 3.4, p. 15 and Remark 3.5, p. 16 (from Grosse-Klönne)
items.note: Used "repeatedly": it is what makes every de Rham row in the fundamental diagrams strictly exact, and it is the reason the answers are Fréchet spaces rather than mere topological vector spaces.

items.name: Finiteness, Hausdorffness and classicality on affine pieces, and strictness of the hypercover system
items.statement: If Y_J is affine then Γ(]Y_J[_{Z_J},Ω^•) has finite dimensional algebraic cohomology with Hausdorff topology and its cohomology H̃^* is classical: by the Poincaré Lemma for an open ball one may assume the tube is the generic fibre of a weak formal lift of Y_J, and then Lemma 3.4 gives that coim d^{i−1} → im d^{i−1} is an isomorphism with closed image in ker d^i. Consequently any map between the de Rham complexes of two embeddings of Y_I is a strict quasi-isomorphism, so for affine Y all arrows of the system defining RΓ_rig(Y/O^0_F) are strict quasi-isomorphisms; the quasi-compact case follows from a finite affine covering.
items.note: This is the technical reason the hocolim definition is independent of choices and the reason topologies can be controlled at all.

items.name: Grosse-Klönne's compactified deformation spaces and the bases r^⁺, r^†
items.statement: Set r^+ := k[T] and r^† := O_F[T]^†, with the log structure associated with T, and r̃ := O_F[T] as lifting base; Frobenius on r^† is T ↦ T^p. For a log-scheme X over r^+ the complex RΓ_rig(X/r^†) ∈ D(C_F) is constructed exactly as RΓ_rig(Y/O^0_F), with exactifications over r̃, weak completions X_J of X̃_J and Ω^•_{X_J/r^†} the weak completion of Ω^•_{X̃_J/r̃}; the same works for log-schemes with boundary. For a semistable X_0 with irreducible components {X_i}_{i∈I}, M_• denotes the nerve of ⊔_i X_i → X_0 and M_J = ∩_{j∈J} X_j. To M = M_J, Grosse-Klönne attaches log-schemes with boundary (P^{J′}_M, V^{J′}_M), ∅ ≠ J′ ⊆ J: heuristically V^{J′}_M is a vector bundle on M built from the log structure of J′, compactified by a direct sum of projective space bundles P^{J′}_M. These glue to a simplicial r^+-log-scheme with boundary (P_•,V_•), and one sets RΓ_rig(X_0/r^†) := RΓ_rig((P_•,V_•)/r^†); there is also a simplicial M′_• over k^0 with M_• → M′_• → (P_•,V_•).
items.note: The point of the compactification is that the cohomology of the structure sheaf of the new deformation space is trivial, which is what makes the Hyodo–Kato isomorphism available overconvergently; the classical construction uses r^PD_ϖ instead. Example 3.10 works this out for a node in dimension 1, where the deformation space is (P^1 × P^1)^an.

items.name: Lemma 3.8, Proposition 3.9 and Proposition 3.12: the deformation-space comparison and both specialisations
items.statement: Lemma 3.8: for O = O^0_F or O^×_K the natural map RΓ_rig(X_0/O) → RΓ_rig(M_•/O) is a strict quasi-isomorphism (the tube of a closed subscheme covered by closed subschemes is the corresponding admissible union, so the two simplicial de Rham complexes agree; strictness because both sides have finite dimensional Hausdorff cohomology). Proposition 3.9: for ∅ ≠ J′ ⊆ J ⊆ I and O_F(0) = O^0_F, O_F(ϖ) = O^×_K (so F(0) = F, F(ϖ) = K), the map RΓ_rig((P^{J′}_M,V^{J′}_M)/r^†) ⊗_F F(a) → RΓ_rig(M/O_F(a)), a = 0, ϖ, given by restricting to the zero section and sending T ↦ a, is a strict quasi-isomorphism. Proposition 3.12: consequently, for a = 0, ϖ the natural maps RΓ_rig(X_0/O_F(a)) → RΓ_rig(M′_•/O_F(a)) ← RΓ_rig(X_0/r^†) ⊗_F F(a) are strict quasi-isomorphisms.
items.locator: Lemma 3.8 and Proposition 3.9, p. 17; Proposition 3.12, p. 18 (Grosse-Klönne, Theorems 3.1 and 3.4)
items.note: These are the statements that make the two specialisations T ↦ 0 and T ↦ ϖ comparable, and hence produce the Hyodo–Kato map as a zigzag.

items.name: Overconvergent Hyodo–Kato cohomology and the Hyodo–Kato isomorphism
items.statement: For X a semistable weak formal scheme over O_K one defines RΓ_HK(X_0) := RΓ_rig(X_0/O^0_F) ∈ D(C_F), with φ and N as above, and the Hyodo–Kato map as the zigzag RΓ_HK(X_0) = RΓ_rig(X_0/O^0_F) ←≅ RΓ_rig(X_0/r^†) → RΓ_rig(X_0/r^†) ⊗_F K ≅→ RΓ_rig(X_0/O^×_K) ≅ RΓ_dR(X_K), using Proposition 3.12. It yields the overconvergent Hyodo–Kato strict quasi-isomorphism ι_HK : RΓ_HK(X_0) ⊗_F K ≅→ RΓ_dR(X_K). Like its classical counterpart it depends on the choice of the uniformiser ϖ, in the usual way (Tsuji, Prop. 4.4.17).
items.note: This is the ι_HK of Theorem 1.8 and of every fundamental diagram in the paper. CR.6 plans the Hyodo–Kato-to-log-de-Rham map for proper semistable models after a field extension and choice of uniformiser, with the change-of-uniformiser formula; this overconvergent version for non-proper X is what the atlas lacks.

items.name: The bases r^+_ϖ, r^PD_ϖ and the period rings Â_st, B̂^+_st, A_cr,K
items.statement: r^+_ϖ := O_F[[T]] with the log structure of T; T ↦ ϖ gives a surjection r^+_ϖ → O^×_K, and r^PD_ϖ is the p-adic divided power envelope of its kernel, with φ(T) = T^p and N(T) = T. Following Tsuji, Â_st,n := H^0_cr(O^×_{C,n}/r^PD_{ϖ,n}), Â_st := lim←_n Â_st,n and B̂^+_st := Â_st[1/p], a Banach F-space (topologically much easier to handle than B^+_st). Â_st,n carries G_K, φ and N, receives compatible maps from A_cr,n and r^PD_{ϖ,n}, and sits in the exact sequence 0 → A_cr,n → Â_st,n —N→ Â_st,n → 0. It is the ring of the PD-envelope of Spec O^×_{C,n} ↪ Spec(A^×_{cr,n} ⊗_{O_{F,n}} r^+_{ϖ,n}), so Spec O^×_{C,1} ↪ Spec Â_st,n is a PD-thickening and Â_st,n ≅ RΓ_cr(O^×_{C,n}/r^PD_{ϖ,n}). There is a canonical B^+_cr-linear isomorphism B^+_st ≅ B̂^{+,N-nilp}_st compatible with G_K, φ and N. Similarly A_cr,K,n := H^0_cr(O^×_{C,n}/O^×_{K,n}) with F^r A_cr,K,n := H^0_cr(O^×_{C,n}/O^×_{K,n}, J^{[r]}), H^i_cr(O^×_{C,n}/O^×_{K,n},J^{[r]}) = 0 for i ≥ 1, and gr^r_F A_cr,n → gr^r_F A_cr,K,n a p^a-quasi-isomorphism with a ≈ v_p(d_{K/F}); B^+_cr,K := A_cr,K[1/p]. Finally there is a natural G_K-equivariant ι : B̂^+_st → B^+_dR built from p_ϖ : B̂^+_st → B^+_cr,K and the comparison of the graded quotients, whose composite with B^+_st → B̂^+_st is the ι_ϖ of §1.4.2.
items.note: The identification of period rings as crystalline cohomology of base rings (Â_st,n ≅ RΓ_cr(O^×_{C,n}/r^PD_{ϖ,n}), A_cr ≅ RΓ_cr(O_C)) is exactly what makes the Künneth maps of §3.3 and §4 possible; CP.0 fixes the normalisation of the rings themselves but not these crystalline interpretations. The printed chain defining ι repeats B^+_cr/F^r where B^+_dR/F^r is meant, and the next sentence writes B̂^+_dR for B^+_dR; recorded in sourceIssues.

items.name: Overconvergent geometric syntomic cohomology and the derived eigenspace [·]^{N=0,φ=p^r}
items.statement: For X a semistable weak formal scheme over O_K and r ≥ 0 set HK(X_C,r) := [RΓ_HK(X_0) ⊗̂^R_F B̂^+_st]^{N=0,φ=p^r} and DR(X_C,r) := (RΓ_dR(X_K) ⊗̂^R_K B^+_dR)/F^r, where F^r(RΓ_dR(X_K) ⊗̂^R_K B^+_dR) := hocolim_{i+j ≥ r} F^i RΓ_dR(X_K) ⊗̂^R_K F^j B^+_dR, and define RΓ_syn(X_C,Q_p(r)) := [HK(X_C,r) —ι_HK⊗ι→ DR(X_C,r)] as a mapping fibre in D(C_{Q_p}). Here [C]^{N=0,φ=p^r} is the homotopy limit of the square with horizontal maps φ − p^r and pφ − p^r and vertical maps N, which commutes because Nφ = pφN; square brackets denote derived eigenspaces and round brackets the non-derived ones.
items.note: This "Bloch–Kato style" definition, out of overconvergent Hyodo–Kato and de Rham data, is what makes the fundamental diagram easy; the Fontaine–Messing definition of §3.3 is what maps to étale cohomology, and Theorem 4.1 compares the two.

items.name: Example 3.16 and Lemma 3.20: the cohomology of RΓ_HK ⊗̂^R B̂^+_st for quasi-compact X
items.statement: For X quasi-compact, RΓ_HK(X_0) ⊗̂^R_F B̂^+_st has classical cohomology and H̃^i(RΓ_HK(X_0) ⊗̂^R_F B̂^+_st) ≅ H^i_HK(X_0) ⊗̂_F B̂^+_st, a finite rank free B̂^+_st-module (proved by induction along the truncations τ^{≥i}, using that each H^i_HK(X_0) is finite dimensional so that ⊗̂ computes ⊗̂^R). Consequently H̃^i(HK(X_C,r)) ≅ (H^i_HK(X_0) ⊗̂_F B̂^+_st)^{N=0,φ=p^r} for i ≥ 0, and these are Banach spaces; in particular H̃^i(HK(X_C,r)) is classical.
items.note: The proof splits the long exact sequences of N and of φ − p^r using the two fundamental exact sequences (3.21) below.

items.name: The two fundamental exact sequences for a finite (φ,N)-module, and the trivialisation exp(Nu)
items.statement: For a finite (φ,N)-module M over F there are short exact sequences 0 → M ⊗_F B^+_cr —β→ M ⊗_F B̂^+_st —N→ M ⊗_F B̂^+_st → 0 and 0 → (M ⊗_F B^+_cr)^{φ=p^r} → M ⊗_F B^+_cr —(p^r − φ)→ M ⊗_F B^+_cr → 0. The first follows by induction on the nilpotency order of N from the case M = F (the rationalisation of 0 → A_cr,n → Â_st,n → Â_st,n → 0); β is the Frobenius-equivariant trivialisation m ⊗ b ↦ exp(Nu)·m ⊗ b, an isomorphism M ⊗ B^+_cr ≅ (M ⊗ B̂^+_st)^{N=0} which is not Galois equivariant. The second is Colmez–Nizioł, Remark 2.30.
items.note: These sequences, and the fact that the trivialisation is not Galois equivariant, are used in Lemmas 3.20, 3.28 and 3.39 and in the change of period ring (3.37).

items.name: Lemmas 3.26 and 3.28: the Stein case, classicality, and the Banach–Colmez Mittag-Leffler argument
items.statement: Let X be Stein with Stein covering {U_n}. Then RΓ_HK(X_0) ⊗̂^R_F B̂^+_st ≅ holim_n (RΓ_HK(U_{n,0}) ⊗̂^R_F B̂^+_st), the cohomology is classical, and H̃^i(RΓ_HK(X_0) ⊗̂^R_F B̂^+_st) ≅ H^i_HK(X_0) ⊗̂_F B̂^+_st ≅ lim←_n (H^i_HK(U_{n,0}) ⊗̂_F B̂^+_st). Moreover H̃^i([RΓ_HK(X_0) ⊗̂^R_F B̂^+_st]^{N=0,φ=p^r}) is classical and equals (H^i_HK(X_0) ⊗̂_F B̂^+_st)^{N=0,φ=p^r}, a Fréchet space, and H̃^i([RΓ_HK(X_0) ⊗̂^R_F B̂^+_st]^{N=0}) ≅ H^i_HK(X_0) ⊗̂_F B^+_cr (not Galois equivariantly). The vanishing of the first derived limits uses the Mittag-Leffler criterion in convex spaces; for the φ-eigenspaces it uses that the system {(H^i_HK(U_{n,0}) ⊗̂_F B^+_cr)^{φ=p^r}} lifts to finite dimensional Banach–Colmez spaces whose Dimensions decrease lexicographically and stabilise because heights of BC subspaces are ≥ 0.
items.locator: the discussion of (3.24)–(3.25) and Lemmas 3.26 and 3.28, §3.2.2, pp. 21–22
items.note: VB3 constructs Banach–Colmez spaces ("Banach–Colmez geometry without circular classification") with their Dimension formalism, which is exactly the input used here and in Lemma 3.39 and Remark 3.41; the Mittag-Leffler argument for systems of BC spaces is the paper's own contribution. Independent review: VB3 supplies geometric Banach–Colmez constructions, not this Stein inverse-limit theorem nor the exact classical Dimension/height bridge it uses.
items.statusReview: VB3 supplies geometric Banach–Colmez constructions, not this Stein inverse-limit theorem nor the exact classical Dimension/height bridge it uses.

items.name: Example 3.30: explicit computation of the de Rham term DR(X_C,r) and strictness of its differentials
items.statement: Let X be affine or Stein, so that Ω^i(X_K) is an LB-space resp. a Fréchet space and H̃^i_dR(X_K) is classical. In the Stein case F^r(RΓ_dR(X_K) ⊗̂^R_K B^+_dR) ≅ F^r(Ω^•(X_K) ⊗̂_K B^+_dR) = (O(X_K) ⊗̂_K F^r B^+_dR → Ω^1(X_K) ⊗̂_K F^{r−1}B^+_dR → ⋯) and DR(X_C,r) ≅ (O(X_K) ⊗̂_K (B^+_dR/F^r) → Ω^1(X_K) ⊗̂_K (B^+_dR/F^{r−1}) → ⋯ → Ω^{r−1}(X_K) ⊗̂_K (B^+_dR/F^1)); in particular DR(X_C,0) = 0, DR(X_C,1) ≅ O(X_K) ⊗̂_K C and DR(X_C,2) ≅ (O(X_K) ⊗̂_K (B^+_dR/F^2) → Ω^1(X_K) ⊗̂_K C). The differentials are strict (each factors as a strict surjection Id ⊗ can followed by d^i ⊗ Id), so H̃^i DR(X_C,r) is classical and Fréchet. In the affine case the same formulas hold with B^+_dR replaced by B^+_dR/F^r, H̃^i DR(X_C,r) is classical and LB and vanishes for i ≥ r, and the LB property is proved from the strict exact sequences 0 → Ω^i(X_C)/im d^{i−1} → H^i DR(X_C,r) → H^i_dR(X_K) ⊗̂_K (B^+_dR/F^{r−i−1}) → 0 and 0 → Ω^i(X_K) ⊗̂_K gr^{r−i−1}_F B^+_dR → ker d̃^i → ker d^i ⊗̂_K (B^+_dR/F^{r−i−1}) → 0, together with the fact that a Hausdorff quotient of a Hausdorff LB-space is LB and that ker d^i is of compact type.
items.note: This is where all the functional analysis of §2 is actually spent: Lemma 2.3 in both its cases, the interchange of ⊗̂ with limits, compact-type spaces and Emerton's LB-quotient theorem.

items.name: Example 3.34: syntomic cohomology in degrees 0 and 1
items.statement: Let X be affine or Stein and geometrically irreducible. For r = 0, H̃^0_syn(X_C,Q_p) ≅ (H^0_HK(X_0) ⊗̂_F B^+_st)^{N=0,φ=1} ≅ (B^+_cr)^{φ=1} = Q_p, so it is classical. For r = 1 there is an exact sequence H^0 HK(X_C,1) —ι_HK⊗ι→ O(X_K) ⊗̂_K C → H̃^1_syn(X_C,Q_p(1)) → (H^1_HK(X_0) ⊗̂_F B̂^+_st)^{φ=p,N=0} → 0; since H^0_HK(X_0) = F one has H^0 HK(X_C,1) = (B^+_cr)^{φ=p}, and the fundamental exact sequence 0 → Q_p(1) → (B^+_cr)^{φ=p} → B^+_dR/F^1 → 0 turns this into 0 → C → O(X_C) —∂→ H̃^1_syn(X_C,Q_p(1)) → (H^1_HK(X_0) ⊗̂_F B̂^+_st)^{φ=p,N=0} → 0, so H̃^1_syn(X_C,Q_p(1)) is classical.
items.note: The r = 0 line is printed with the exponent φ = p instead of φ = 1, which would make the identification with Q_p false; recorded in sourceIssues.

items.name: Proposition 3.36: the fundamental diagram for overconvergent syntomic cohomology
items.statement: Let X be an affine or Stein semistable weak formal scheme and r ≥ 0. There is a natural map of strictly exact sequences from 0 → Ω^{r−1}(X_C)/ker d —∂→ H^r_syn(X_C,Q_p(r)) → (H^r_HK(X_0) ⊗̂_F B^+_st)^{N=0,φ=p^r} → 0 to 0 → Ω^{r−1}(X_C)/ker d —d→ Ω^r(X_C)^{d=0} → H^r_dR(X_K) ⊗̂_K C → 0, with the identity on the left, β in the middle and ι_HK ⊗ θ on the right, where ι_HK ⊗ θ is induced by RΓ_HK(X_0) ⊗̂_F B̂^+_st —ι_HK⊗ι→ RΓ_dR(X_K) ⊗̂_K B^+_dR —θ→ RΓ_dR(X_K) ⊗̂_K C and β is induced by RΓ_syn(X_C,Q_p(r)) → F^r(RΓ_dR(X_K) ⊗̂^R_K B^+_dR) —θ→ (0 → Ω^r(X_K) ⊗̂_K C → ⋯). Moreover ker(ι_HK ⊗ θ) ≅ (H^r_HK(X_0) ⊗̂_F B^+_st)^{N=0,φ=p^{r−1}}, H^r_syn(X_C,Q_p(r)) is LB in the affine case and Fréchet in the Stein case, and β and ι_HK ⊗ θ are strict with closed images.
items.locator: Proposition 3.36, §3.2.3, pp. 25–27 (case r = 1 worked out in Example 3.35, p. 25)
items.note: This is the syntomic fundamental diagram; Theorem 4.12 (= Theorem 1.8) is its transport to pro-étale cohomology along α_FM, ι_BK and ι_rig. The proof first replaces B^+_st by B̂^+_st through the trivialisation (3.37), then uses Lemma 3.39 and the slope bound. Independent review: The β target has Ω^r in cohomological degree r (preceded by r zero terms); it is the stupid filtration of the de Rham complex, not a complex putting Ω^r in degree 1 for all r.

items.name: Lemma 3.39 and the slope bound: exactness of the t-multiplication sequence and surjectivity of ι_HK ⊗ θ
items.statement: Call a (φ,N)-module effective if all Frobenius slopes are ≥ 0. For M an effective finite (φ,N)-module over F the sequence 0 → (M ⊗_F B̂^+_st)^{φ=p^j,N=0} —t→ (M ⊗_F B̂^+_st)^{φ=p^{j+1},N=0} —1⊗θ→ M ⊗_F C is exact, and the right-hand map is surjective if the slopes are ≤ j. The proof transports the sequence by the trivialisation (3.22) (using θ(u) = 0) to 0 → (M ⊗_F B^+_cr)^{φ=p^j} —t→ (M ⊗_F B^+_cr)^{φ=p^{j+1}} —1⊗θ→ M ⊗_F C, reduces exactness in the middle to (F^1 B^+_cr)^{φ=p^n} = (t B^+_cr)^{φ=p^n} — which follows from (F^1B^+_cr)^{φ=p^n} ⊆ {x : θ(φ^k(x)) = 0 for all k ≥ 0} = tB^+_cr — and proves surjectivity by computing the Dimension of the cokernel of multiplication by t in finite dimensional Banach–Colmez spaces: Σ_{r_i ≤ j+1}(j+1−r_i,1) − Σ_{r_i ≤ j}(j−r_i,1) = (dim_F M, 0), which is the Dimension of M ⊗_F C. For X quasi-compact the slopes of Frobenius on H^i_HK(X_0) are ≤ i, by the weight spectral sequence and the classical bound for smooth k-schemes.
items.locator: Lemma 3.39 with footnote 23, pp. 26–27, and the slope argument on p. 27
items.note: The Dimension computation is BC-space arithmetic, which VB3 owns; the slope bound is Chiarellotto–Le Stum. Remark 3.41 makes the failure of surjectivity in degree r precise: the image of ι_HK ⊗ θ is the C-points of the cokernel of multiplication by t, of Dimension Σ_{r_i ≤ r−1}(1,0) + Σ_{r−1 < r_i ≤ r}(r−r_i,1). Independent review: The effective (φ,N)-module fundamental sequence, slope bound and its classical Banach–Colmez Dimension proof are not stated in VB3.
items.statusReview: The effective (φ,N)-module fundamental sequence, slope bound and its classical Banach–Colmez Dimension proof are not stated in VB3.

items.name: Semistable p-adic formal schemes without self-intersections
items.statement: A p-adic formal scheme X over O_K is semistable if locally for the Zariski topology X = Spf(R) with R the p-adic completion of an algebra étale over O_K{T_1,…,T_n}/(T_1⋯T_m − ϖ); self-intersections are not allowed. It carries the log structure induced by the special fibre, and one writes X_{O_C} for its base change.
items.note: Contrast §3.1.1, where semistable weak formal schemes may have self-intersections. The distinction matters because the crystalline constructions of §3.3 are made on formal, not weak formal, schemes.

items.name: Fontaine–Messing syntomic cohomology of a formal scheme, integrally and with Q_p(r)-coefficients
items.statement: For r ≥ 0 and X = X_{O_C}, RΓ_syn(X,Z/p^n(r)) := [F^r RΓ_cr(X_n) —φ−p^r→ RΓ_cr(X_n)] with F^r RΓ_cr(X_n) := RΓ_cr(X_n,J^{[r]}) and absolute crystalline cohomology (over O_{F,n}), and RΓ_syn(X,Z_p(r)) := holim_n RΓ_syn(X,Z/p^n(r)); rationally RΓ_syn(X,Z_p(r))_{Q_p} = [F^r RΓ_cr(X)_{Q_p} → RΓ_cr(X)_{Q_p}] = [RΓ_cr(X)^{φ=p^r}_{Q_p} → RΓ_cr(X)_{Q_p}/F^r]. For the pro-étale theory one instead sheafifies: A_cr := (U ↦ (holim_n RΓ_cr(U_n))_{Q_p}), F^r A_cr, S(r) := (U ↦ RΓ_syn(U,Z_p(r))_{Q_p}) on affine Zariski opens U of X, and sets RΓ_cr(X,Q_p) := RΓ(X,A_cr), RΓ_syn(X,Q_p(r)) := RΓ(X,S(r)) = [F^rRΓ_cr(X,Q_p) → RΓ_cr(X,Q_p)] = [RΓ_cr(X,Q_p)^{φ=p^r} → RΓ_cr(X,Q_p)/F^r]. There is a natural map RΓ_syn(X,Z_p(r))_{Q_p} → RΓ_syn(X,Q_p(r)), a quasi-isomorphism when X is of finite type but not in general, because the first inverts p only at the end while the second inverts it on every U. Both are topologised with crystalline embedding systems, becoming complexes of Banach Q_p-spaces for X quasi-compact.
items.note: D.2 constructs "filtered de Rham complexes, Frobenius data and the syntomic mapping fibre" and the comparison with the étale regulator in the smooth unramified setting; what this paper adds is the semistable formal-scheme version over O_C, the sheafified Q_p(r)-variant and the gluing over a Stein exhaustion — and the observation that the two versions differ for non-quasi-compact X. Independent review: D.2 is restricted to its smooth/unramified regulator setting; it does not own the semistable O_C construction, sheafwise rationalization or non-quasi-compact comparison.
items.statusReview: D.2 is restricted to its smooth/unramified regulator setting; it does not own the semistable O_C construction, sheafwise rationalization or non-quasi-compact comparison.

items.name: Proposition 3.45 and Corollary 3.46: the Fontaine–Messing period map to étale and pro-étale cohomology
items.statement: For X a semistable finite type formal scheme over O_K, the Fontaine–Messing period map α_FM : RΓ_syn(X,Q_p(r)) → RΓ_ét(X_C,Q_p(r)) is a quasi-isomorphism after truncation τ^{≤r} (Fontaine–Messing, via Tsuji and Colmez–Nizioł; one uses the version compatible with Chern classes). For X semistable but not necessarily of finite type there is a natural period map α_FM : RΓ_syn(X,Q_p(r)) → RΓ_proét(X_C,Q_p(r)) which is a strict quasi-isomorphism after τ^{≤r}. The proof covers X by quasi-compacts, gets strictness from Lemma 2.1 because locally the period map is a zigzag of complexes of Banach spaces, and then compares étale with pro-étale cohomology: with Z/p^n-coefficients this is Scholze's Cor. 3.17, and one passes to Z_p and to Q_p using that RΓ commutes with holim, that RΓ_proét(X_C,holim_n Z/p^n(r)) ≅ RΓ_proét(X_C,lim←_n Z/p^n(r)), and that the pro-étale site of a quasi-compact rigid space is coherent, so cohomology commutes with colimits.
items.locator: Proposition 3.45, p. 28 and Corollary 3.46 with (3.47), p. 29
items.note: A1 builds the pro-étale site with Scholze's corrected covering definition, and H1 the formal models, specialisation and nearby-cycle comparison; the comparison of étale with pro-étale cohomology and the period map itself are not planned. This proposition is Proposition 1.11, the starting point of both computations. Independent review: A1 constructs sites and H1 the specified formal/adic nearby-cycle comparisons. Neither asserts this Fontaine–Messing p-adic period map or its uniform p-power bound.
items.statusReview: A1 constructs sites and H1 the specified formal/adic nearby-cycle comparisons. Neither asserts this Fontaine–Messing p-adic period map or its uniform p-power bound.

items.name: Crystalline syntomic cohomology à la Bloch–Kato and the comparison ι_BK
items.statement: For X a semistable formal scheme over O_K and r ≥ 0 define, in D(C_{Q_p}), RΓ^{BK}_syn(X_{O_C},Q_p(r)) := [[RΓ_cr(X/r^PD_ϖ,Q_p) ⊗̂^R_{r^PD_{ϖ,Q_p}} B̂^+_st]^{N=0,φ=p^r} —p_ϖ⊗ι→ (RΓ_dR(X_K) ⊗̂^R_K B^+_dR)/F^r]. Since r^PD_{ϖ,Q_p} is not a field, the completed tensor product is defined for X of finite type by (RΓ_cr(X/r^PD_ϖ) ⊗̂_{r^PD_ϖ} Â_st) ⊗^L Q_p, taken in D(Ind(PD_{Q_p})), and extended to general X by étale cohomological descent. Proposition 3.48: there is a functorial quasi-isomorphism ι_BK : RΓ^{BK}_syn(X_{O_C},Q_p(r)) ≅→ RΓ_syn(X_{O_C},Q_p(r)). It is induced by a pair of Künneth-type maps ι^1_BK and ι^2_BK making a square commute: ι^1_BK comes from the zigzag RΓ_cr(X/r^PD_ϖ,Q_p) ⊗̂^R B̂^+_st —∪→ RΓ_cr(X_{O_C}/r^PD_ϖ,Q_p) ← RΓ_cr(X_{O_C},Q_p), whose cup product is a quasi-isomorphism (Tsuji, Prop. 4.5.4) because X_{O_K̄,n} → O^×_{K̄,n} is log-syntomic, taken on N = 0 parts using Kato's monodromy triangle RΓ_cr(X_{O_K̄,n}/O_{F,n}) → RΓ_cr(X_{O_K̄,n}/r^PD_{ϖ,n}) —N→ RΓ_cr(X_{O_K̄,n}/r^PD_{ϖ,n}); ι^2_BK comes from the analogous Künneth map over O^×_K, where the base change from O_F to O^×_K is a quasi-isomorphism up to a universal constant (Nekovář–Nizioł, Cor. 2.4).
items.note: This is the step that converts the Fontaine–Messing definition, good for period maps but useless for computation, into one built from Hyodo–Kato and de Rham data. The "technical heart of the paper" described in §1.3.1.

items.name: Theorem 4.1: the overconvergent and crystalline syntomic cohomologies agree for Stein spaces
items.statement: Let X be a semistable weak formal scheme over O_K with associated formal scheme X̂, and r ≥ 0. There is a functorial map in D(C_{Q_p}) ι_rig : RΓ_syn(X_C,Q_p(r)) → RΓ^{BK}_syn(X̂_{O_C},Q_p(r)), and it is a quasi-isomorphism if X is Stein. It is induced by a pair (ι^1_rig, ι^2_rig): ι^2_rig is the map from de Rham cohomology of a weak formal scheme to that of its completion, an isomorphism for X Stein because the coherent cohomology of a partially proper dagger space agrees with that of its rigid avatar (Grosse-Klönne, Theorem 2.26); ι^1_rig is the composite of the change-of-convergence map RΓ_rig(X_0/O^0_F) ⊗̂^R_F B̂^+_st → RΓ_cr(X_0/O^0_F,F) ⊗̂^R_F B̂^+_st with the inverse of h_cr, and is compatible with monodromy.
items.note: Together with Corollary 3.46 and Proposition 3.48 this is what transports the syntomic fundamental diagram to pro-étale cohomology; the Stein hypothesis enters exactly twice, through the dagger-to-rigid comparison and through the change-of-topology map below.

items.name: Remark 4.4 and Proposition 4.5: convergent cohomology, and rigid = convergent when the components are proper
items.statement: Relative convergent cohomology is well developed (Ogus, Shiho): its site is defined like the crystalline one with PD-thickenings replaced by enlargements — p-adic formal schemes, analytically closed discs of any radius < 1 rather than of a fixed radius — and convergent cohomology is the cohomology of the rational structure sheaf on it. It is invariant under homeomorphic exact closed immersions; a Poincaré lemma computes it locally by de Rham complexes of convergent tubes of log-smooth formal log-schemes, with open discs replacing the fixed closed discs of the crystalline theory; and the natural map to crystalline cohomology is a quasi-isomorphism for log-schemes log-smooth over the reduction of the base, so RΓ_conv(X_0/O^0_F) ≅ RΓ_cr(X_0/O^0_F,F) for X_0 semistable. Proposition 4.5 (Grosse-Klönne, Theorem 5.3): if all irreducible components of X_0 are proper then RΓ_rig(X_0/O^0_F) → RΓ_conv(X_0/O^0_F) is a quasi-isomorphism, by comparing the two weight spectral sequences and the classical statement H^*_rig(S/O_F) ≅ H^*_conv(S/O_F) for S smooth and proper over k.
items.note: Convergent cohomology with enlargements, its Poincaré lemma and its comparison with crystalline cohomology are the subject of the Part II proposed by PAPER-KISIN-MADAPUSIPERA-SHIN-22 ("CrystallineCohomologyConvergentPartII"); this paper is a consumer, and needs in addition the logarithmic and overconvergent comparison.

items.name: The change-of-convergence and change-of-topology maps are strict quasi-isomorphisms for Stein X
items.statement: The map RΓ_rig(X_0/O^0_F) ⊗̂^R_F B̂^+_st → RΓ_cr(X_0/O^0_F,F) ⊗̂^R_F B̂^+_st is compatible with Frobenius and monodromy, and for X Stein it is a strict quasi-isomorphism; it suffices to prove this for RΓ_rig(X_0/O^0_F) → RΓ_cr(X_0/O^0_F,F), which factors through RΓ_conv(X_0/O^0_F). With the exhaustion {U_s},{Y_s} of §3.1.1 one has strict quasi-isomorphisms RΓ_rig(X_0/O^0_F) ≅ holim_s RΓ_rig(U_s/O^0_F) ≅ holim_s RΓ_rig(Y_s/O^0_F) and RΓ_cr(X_0/O^0_F,F) ≅ holim_s RΓ_cr(U_s/O^0_F,F) ≅ holim_s RΓ_cr(Y_s/O^0_F,F) (the latter because it is a quasi-isomorphism of complexes of Fréchet spaces), so it remains to treat each Y_s, which is proper and ideally log-smooth over k^0: then the convergent-to-crystalline map is a quasi-isomorphism and the rigid-to-convergent map is one by Proposition 4.5.
items.note: This is where "Stein" is used to reduce a statement about a non-proper space to statements about the proper pieces Y_s of its special fibre — the mechanism that the whole paper turns on.

items.name: The map h_cr and the vanishing of the divided-power contribution
items.statement: Let J = ker(p_0 : r^PD_ϖ → O_F, T ↦ 0), a Frobenius- and monodromy-compatible map. From 0 → J_n → r^PD_{ϖ,n} → O_{F,n} → 0, tensoring with the flat Â_st,n and passing to the limit gives 0 → E → Â_st —p_0→ O_F ⊗̂_{r^PD_ϖ} Â_st → 0 with E := J ⊗̂_{r^PD_ϖ} Â_st. Tensoring with RΓ_cr(X_n/r^PD_{ϖ,n}) and with RΓ_cr(X_0/O^0_{F,n}) gives two distinguished triangles with quasi-isomorphic last terms, because RΓ_cr(X_n/r^PD_{ϖ,n}) ⊗^L_{r^PD_{ϖ,n}} O_{F,n} → RΓ_cr(X_0/O^0_{F,n}) is a quasi-isomorphism by a local computation. The complexes [E_{Q_p} ⊗̂^R RΓ_cr(X̂/r^PD_ϖ,Q_p)]^{φ=p^r} and [E_{Q_p} ⊗̂^R_F RΓ_cr(X_0/O^0_F,F)]^{φ=p^r} are strictly acyclic — in fact isomorphic to the trivial complex — because Frobenius is highly topologically nilpotent on J, so p^r − φ is rationally invertible. Hence the resulting two maps are strict quasi-isomorphisms and h_cr is defined as their zigzag; it is compatible with the monodromy operator. The same construction with rig in place of cr and r^† in place of r^PD_ϖ gives h_rig, compatibly.
items.note: The nilpotence of Frobenius on the divided-power ideal is the trick that removes the deformation variable T; the same argument reappears in Corollary 7.6 and in Lemma 7.8.

items.name: Compatibility of ι^1_rig and ι^2_rig: the maps f_1, f_2 and a strict acyclicity of Čech complexes of overconvergent functions
items.statement: Compatibility is checked on a diagram relating the five objects [RΓ_rig(X_0/O^0_F) ⊗̂^R_F B̂^+_st]^{φ=p^r}, the two versions of [RΓ_rig(X_0/r^†) ⊗̂^R_F B̂^+_st]^{φ=p^r} (the (P_•,V_•)-definition and the §3.1.3 one), [RΓ_cr(X_0/O^0_F,F) ⊗̂^R_F B̂^+_st]^{φ=p^r} and [RΓ_cr(X̂/r^PD_ϖ,Q_p) ⊗̂^R B̂^+_st]^{φ=p^r}, together with the de Rham terms. Here f_2 : RΓ_rig(X_0/r^†) → RΓ_conv(X_0/r̂) ←≅ RΓ_conv(X_1/r̂) → RΓ_cr(X̂/r^PD_ϖ,Q_p) with r̂ := O_F{T}, the middle map being an isomorphism by invariance of convergent cohomology under infinitesimal thickenings; and f_1 is induced by RΓ_rig((P_•,V_•)/r^†) → RΓ_rig(M′_•/r^†) ≅ RΓ_rig(M_•/r^†) ← RΓ_rig(X_0/r^†), whose last quasi-isomorphism is strict: one may assume X_0 affine, lift it log-smoothly to r^†, and then, the sheaf of differentials being free, reduce to the strict acyclicity of the Čech complex of overconvergent functions for the covering by the components, which is an inductive limit of strictly acyclic Čech complexes of rigid affinoids (acyclicity plus the open mapping theorem for Banach spaces) along an acyclic inductive system.
items.locator: part (ii) of the proof of Theorem 4.1, §4.1, p. 34
