independentReview.reason: Reject pending a joint contract with the proposal in PAPER-DING-25. Reusing its identifier is appropriate, but that proposal is not an accepted library/atlas supplier. State coefficient and Q_p-analytic versus K-analytic conventions, separate the general locally analytic foundation from Steinberg-specific results, and import the smooth carrier from SR.0/2. Remark citations alone do not supply the Orlik–Strauch/Orlik–Schraen proof chain or APIs.

routes.reason: CR.5 owns log structures, charts and the standard semistable chart, and says to carry the log structure along under reduction and completion — the three log structures on Spf O_K and the base O^0_F are its objects. CR.6 owns the Hyodo–Kato complex of a proper semistable model with Frobenius, the monodromy N and the relation Nφ = pφN in a fixed convention, which is the convention this paper extends to the overconvergent, non-proper setting. CR.4 ("Ordinary and relative de Rham–Witt complexes") owns W_nΩ with restriction, Frobenius, Verschiebung, Teichmüller lifts and dlog, which §6 uses throughout; the logarithmic sheaves WΩ^j_log and the theory of ordinary log schemes are not there, and the paper is a source for them.

independentReview.reason: Reject this mixed source route: CR.5 covers the elementary log bases, but CR.6 is proper and CR.4 does not assert ordinarity of log schemes. The two broader bundled items are now missing. Separate a narrow CR.5 source from explicit continuation contracts for the new HK and log-Witt/ordinarity results.

routes.reason: CP.0 constructs all the ring maps to A_cris, B_cris, B_st and B_dR from the shared objects and fixes the normalisation dictionary for θ, ξ, μ and Frobenius, which is exactly the period-ring input this paper needs (it adds the crystalline interpretations Â_st,n ≅ RΓ_cr(O^×_{C,n}/r^PD_{ϖ,n}) and A_cr ≅ RΓ_cr(O_C) itself). CP.4 owns the semistable B_st comparison for proper flat semistable models, which is the theorem quoted as (4.14) for contrast with the Stein case, and also the compatibility with G_K, φ, N and the filtration that the contrast relies on. PadicHodgeTheory R06.1 owns the period rings themselves.

independentReview.reason: Reject this mixed source route: the period rings are planned by R06.1 with CP.0 normalization, and the proper comparison is CP.4; the Stein pullback in the same item is beyond CP.4. Split the proper theorem from the nonproper continuation and keep the sheafwise versus global rationalization distinction.

routes.reason: D.2 constructs the syntomic mapping fibre from filtered de Rham complexes and Frobenius data, together with a syntomic regulator and its comparison with the étale regulator, in the smooth unramified setting. That is the definition of syntomic cohomology this paper starts from; what it adds is the semistable formal-scheme version over O_C with the divided-power filtration, the sheafified Q_p(r)-variant and the gluing over a Stein exhaustion, and the observation that the integral and rational versions differ when the scheme is not quasi-compact.

independentReview.reason: Reject: D.2’s smooth/unramified regulator construction is a supplier only. The semistable formal O_C Fontaine–Messing construction and two rationalization orders exceed its stated scope.

routes.reason: A1 builds the étale and pro-étale sites of an adic space with Scholze's corrected covering definition, and ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology H1 the formal models, the specialisation morphism and the nearby-cycle comparison. The paper consumes both: its period maps go to pro-étale cohomology of the generic fibre of a formal model, and the comparison of étale with pro-étale cohomology on a quasi-compact rigid space (Scholze, Cor. 3.17 and Prop. 8.2) is quoted in the proof of Corollary 3.46.

independentReview.reason: Reject: an étale/pro-étale site and H1’s nearby-cycle interfaces are not the Fontaine–Messing period theorem. Preserve the corrected Scholze site and prove the coefficient-limit comparison with its separate hypotheses.

routes.reason: VB3 constructs Banach–Colmez geometry with the Dimension formalism. This paper uses it twice in an essential way: to prove that a projective system of φ-eigenspaces is Mittag-Leffler, because the Dimensions of the images decrease lexicographically and heights of subspaces are non-negative (Lemma 3.28), and to prove the surjectivity in Lemma 3.39 by computing the Dimension of the cokernel of multiplication by t; Remark 3.41 measures the failure of surjectivity in degree r the same way.

independentReview.reason: Reject: the VB3 stage describes geometric Banach–Colmez constructions with a carefully staged classification dependency. Neither the classical Dimension/height calculus nor the two specific Stein/eigenspace theorems follows by naming VB3. Require an explicit comparison bridge and independent proof leaves.

routes.reason: ET.6a constructs the Drinfeld tower for arbitrary n over a finite extension of Q_p. This source route supplies only the half-plane definition and its GL2 action as its n=2 base geometry. It neither introduces new tower foundations nor claims the higher-dimensional geometry is absent.

independentReview.reason: Accept only this narrow source route for the finite-K Drinfeld half-plane and GL2 action, already within ET.6a’s arbitrary-n Drinfeld-tower construction. It supplies no new cohomology theorem, no separate definition of a tower, and no claim that higher-dimensional Drinfeld geometry is absent. The original item statement itself has the required K/Q_p finite hypothesis.

routes.reason: RG2.2 owns the local structure theory of a reductive group over a local field, including the parabolic subgroups and the valued Bruhat–Tits data. The paper needs the standard parabolics P_J = B W_J B of GL_{d+1}(K) with their profinite coset spaces G/P_J, and the Bruhat–Tits building of PGL_{d+1}(K) with its lattice-class vertices and its truncations; the identification of those vertices with the irreducible components of the special fibre of the standard model is specific to this geometry and belongs to the Drinfeld route.

independentReview.reason: Reject: RG2.2 owns buildings, not the entire algebraic-parabolic and profinite-flag bundle. Import upstream parabolics without replanning, RG2.0 rational-point topology and RG2.4 Iwasawa decomposition as needed; prove the quotient/profinite topology comparison explicitly.

prerequisites.citation: E. Grosse-Klönne, Frobenius and monodromy operators in rigid analysis, and Drinfeld's symmetric space, J. Algebraic Geom. 14 (2005), 391–437 [32]
prerequisites.why: The most load-bearing input. It supplies the whole overconvergent Hyodo–Kato package: log-rigid cohomology built by hand from embedding systems, the compactified deformation spaces (P^{J′}_M,V^{J′}_M) with the comparison of the two specialisations T ↦ 0 and T ↦ ϖ (its Theorems 3.1 and 3.4, quoted as Propositions 3.9 and 3.12), the weight spectral sequence and finiteness (its Theorem 5.3, quoted as Propositions 3.2 and 4.5), the admissibility of tube coverings, and the standard G-equivariant semistable weak formal model of the Drinfeld half-space (its §6.1) with the computation that Frobenius acts by q^r on its Hyodo–Kato cohomology.

prerequisites.citation: E. Grosse-Klönne, Integral structures in the p-adic holomorphic discrete series, Represent. Theory 9 (2005), 354–384 [33]; Sheaves of bounded p-adic logarithmic differential forms, Ann. Sci. ÉNS 40 (2007), 351–386 [35]; Acyclic coefficient systems on buildings [34]; On special representations of p-adic reductive groups, Duke Math. J. 163 (2014), 2179–2216 [37]
prerequisites.why: The second pillar. [33] and [35] prove the acyclicity of the sheaves of (logarithmic) differentials on the standard model and on its truncations and the vanishing of d on global sections (Propositions 6.3, 6.4, 6.5, 6.7); [34] proves the acyclicity criterion for coefficient systems on the Bruhat–Tits building that Lemma 6.8 extends to the truncations; [37] proves the mod p irreducibility of the generalized Steinberg representation (Proposition 5.1) and the finite generation of Sp_J(O_K) over O_K[G] (Corollary 5.3), which is what turns the integral regulator into an isomorphism in Theorem 6.28.

prerequisites.citation: P. Schneider, U. Stuhler, The cohomology of p-adic symmetric spaces, Invent. Math. 105 (1991), 47–122 [73]
prerequisites.why: The ℓ-adic and de Rham computation the paper reproves p-adically: the axioms a cohomology theory must satisfy, the simplicial complexes built from the Tits building with the computation of their reduced cohomology, the support spectral sequence over the Stein exhaustion, and Theorem 5.8 identifying H^r_ét(H^d_C,Q_ℓ(r)) and H^r_dR(H^d_K) with duals of Steinberg representations.

prerequisites.citation: A. Iovita, M. Spiess, Logarithmic differential forms on p-adic symmetric spaces, Duke Math. J. 110 (2001), 253–278 [47]
prerequisites.why: The description of those isomorphisms by symbols: distributions and measures on the space of hyperplanes, degenerate distributions, the regulator maps and the strict exactness of the regulator sequence (their Theorem 4.5, quoted as Theorem 5.10). Lemma 5.11 is its Hyodo–Kato generalisation, and it is what makes the Hyodo–Kato cohomology of the half-space computable.

prerequisites.citation: O. Hyodo, K. Kato, Semi-stable reduction and crystalline cohomology with logarithmic poles, Astérisque 223 (1994), 221–268 [39]
prerequisites.why: The classical Hyodo–Kato isomorphism, which §7 makes functorial and quantitative: the p^N-inverse of the linearised Frobenius (their 2.24), the Frobenius-equivariant p^{N_ι}-section of the specialisation map (their Prop. 4.13 and Lemma 5.2), and the exact sequence 0 → (Ω^j ⊕ Ω^{j−1})/R^j_n → W_{n+1}Ω^j → W_nΩ^j → 0 (their Theorem 4.4) used in Lemma 6.20.

prerequisites.citation: T. Tsuji, p-adic étale cohomology and crystalline cohomology in the semi-stable reduction case, Invent. Math. 137 (1999), 233–411 [81]
prerequisites.why: The comparison between p-adic nearby cycles and syntomic sheaves behind Propositions 3.45 and 6.1, the Künneth quasi-isomorphism whose proof carries over to (3.49)–(3.50) (his Prop. 4.5.4), the definition of the period rings B̂^+_st and A_cr,K with the p^a-comparison of their graded pieces (his §4.6 and Lemma 4.6.2), the crystalline first Chern classes (his 2.2.3) and the change-of-uniformiser formula for ι_HK (his Prop. 4.4.17).

prerequisites.citation: J.-M. Fontaine, W. Messing, p-adic periods and p-adic étale cohomology, Contemp. Math. 67 (1987), 179–207 [26]
prerequisites.why: Syntomic cohomology as the mapping fibre [F^r RΓ_cr → RΓ_cr] and the integral period map α̃_FM : RΓ_syn(Y,Z_p(r)) → RΓ_ét(Y_C,Z_p(r)′), which is a p^N-quasi-isomorphism after truncation (their III.5). This is the map that connects everything computable in the paper to étale cohomology.

prerequisites.citation: P. Colmez, W. Nizioł, Syntomic complexes and p-adic nearby cycles, Invent. Math. 208 (2017), 1–108 [20]; J. Nekovář, W. Nizioł, Syntomic cohomology and p-adic regulators for varieties over p-adic fields, Algebra Number Theory 10 (2016), 1695–1790 [62]
prerequisites.why: The algebraic model the paper adapts: the Bloch–Kato description of syntomic cohomology for proper algebraic and analytic varieties, the semistable comparison theorem quoted as (4.14), the exact sequence (3.21b), the Dimension calculus for Banach–Colmez spaces used in Lemma 3.39 and Remark 3.41, the base-change comparison up to a universal constant (Nekovář–Nizioł, Cor. 2.4) used for ι^2_BK, the formal definition of the monodromy operator, and the compatibility of the Hyodo–Kato map with Chern classes in the algebraic setting (their Lemma 5.1), which Lemma 7.8 transplants.

prerequisites.citation: P. Scholze, p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties, Forum Math. Pi 1 (2013), e1 [76]
prerequisites.why: The pro-étale site and the comparison of étale with pro-étale cohomology: his Cor. 3.17 (agreement with Z/p^n-coefficients), Prop. 8.2 (the pro-étale cohomology of an inverse limit of constant sheaves) and Prop. 3.12 (coherence of the pro-étale site of a quasi-compact rigid space), all three used in the proof of Corollary 3.46.

prerequisites.citation: P. Colmez, Espaces de Banach de dimension finie, J. Inst. Math. Jussieu 1 (2002), 331–439 [14]; Espaces vectoriels de dimension finie et représentations de de Rham [15]
prerequisites.why: Finite dimensional Banach–Colmez spaces with their Dimension and height: they lift the systems of φ-eigenspaces in Lemma 3.28 so that the Mittag-Leffler property can be proved from the stabilisation of Dimensions, and they give the surjectivity in Lemma 3.39 by a Dimension count. Without them the fundamental diagram would not be exact on the right.

prerequisites.citation: F. Prosmans, Derived categories for functional analysis, Publ. RIMS 36 (2000), 19–83 [70]; J.-P. Schneiders, Quasi-abelian categories and sheaves, Mém. SMF 76 (1999) [75]
prerequisites.why: The quasi-abelian formalism the whole paper is written in: C_K is quasi-abelian with kernels and cokernels computed with the induced topologies, strict maps are the relatively open ones, C_K has enough injectives with injective resolutions by Fréchet or Banach spaces, the Mittag-Leffler acyclicity criterion in convex spaces, and Schneiders' t-structure with its left and right hearts and the notion of strict exactness.

prerequisites.citation: E. Grosse-Klönne, Rigid analytic spaces with overconvergent structure sheaf, J. Reine Angew. Math. 519 (2000), 73–95 [29]; De Rham cohomology of rigid spaces [30]; Compactifications of log morphisms [31]; A. Langer, A. Muralidharan, An analogue of Raynaud's theorem: weak formal schemes and dagger spaces [51]; D. Meredith, Weak formal schemes, Nagoya Math. J. 45 (1972) [57]; A. Vezzani, The Monsky–Washnitzer and the overconvergent realizations [83]
prerequisites.why: Dagger spaces and weak formal schemes: the overconvergent structure sheaf, the equivalence of partially proper dagger and rigid spaces (Theorem 2.27) and the agreement of their coherent cohomology (Theorem 2.26, which makes ι^2_rig an isomorphism), the strictness of the de Rham differentials on a smooth Stein or affinoid dagger space (Lemma 4.7 and [30, Cor. 3.2], quoted as Lemma 3.4), log morphisms with boundary, and the Raynaud-type dictionary between weak formal schemes and dagger spaces.

prerequisites.citation: A. Ogus, The convergent topos in characteristic p, Grothendieck Festschrift III [63]; A. Shiho, Crystalline fundamental groups II [77] and Relative log convergent cohomology and relative rigid cohomology I, arXiv:0707.1742 [78]
prerequisites.why: Relative convergent cohomology with enlargements, its invariance under infinitesimal thickenings (Ogus 0.6.1, Shiho Prop. 3.1), its Poincaré lemma (Shiho Theorem 2.29) and its comparison with crystalline cohomology for log-smooth log schemes (Shiho Theorem 2.36). The paper factors its change-of-topology map through convergent cohomology, so this package is what makes the comparison of overconvergent with crystalline syntomic cohomology possible.

prerequisites.citation: L. Illusie, Complexe de de Rham–Witt et cohomologie cristalline, Ann. Sci. ÉNS 12 (1979), 501–661 [43]; L. Illusie, M. Raynaud, Les suites spectrales associées au complexe de de Rham–Witt [44]; L. Illusie, Ordinarité des intersections complètes générales [45]
prerequisites.why: The de Rham–Witt machinery of §6 and of the appendix: finiteness and freeness of H^*_ét(T,W_nΩ^j), the perfectness of RΓ_ét(T,WΩ^•) with its mod p^n comparison, the structure of Z^j_∞ with Raynaud's finiteness theorem (their 2.5.2–2.5.3, which is Lemma A.1), and the ordinarity of projective bundles and of blow-ups with the weight-spectral-sequence criterion (Illusie's Props 1.4, 1.6, 1.10 and Remark 2.8).

prerequisites.citation: S. Bloch, K. Kato, p-adic étale cohomology, Publ. Math. IHÉS 63 (1986), 107–152 [7]; P. Lorenzon, Logarithmic Hodge–Witt forms and Hyodo–Kato cohomology, J. Algebra 249 (2002), 247–265 [53]
prerequisites.why: The notion of an ordinary (log) scheme and the four equivalent characterisations of ordinarity — through the vanishing of H^*(B^j), the logarithmic differentials, the logarithmic de Rham–Witt sheaves and the bijectivity of the de Rham–Witt Frobenius — which is Proposition 6.9 and the engine of the whole étale computation.

prerequisites.citation: A. Mokrane, La suite spectrale des poids en cohomologie de Hyodo–Kato, Duke Math. J. 72 (1993), 301–337 [58]; Y. Nakkajima, p-adic weight spectral sequences of log varieties [60]; B. Chiarellotto, B. Le Stum, Pentes en cohomologie rigide et F-isocristaux unipotents, Manuscripta Math. 100 (1999) [13]
prerequisites.why: The weight spectral sequence with its Frobenius equivariance, used both for the ordinarity of a semistable scheme with ordinary strata (Proposition 6.12) and, with Chiarellotto–Le Stum's bound that the slopes of Frobenius on H^j_rig of a smooth k-scheme are ≤ j, for the slope hypothesis of Lemma 3.39 — the hypothesis that makes ι_HK ⊗ θ surjective in degree r−1 and hence the fundamental diagram exact.

prerequisites.citation: M. Emerton, Locally analytic vectors in representations of locally analytic p-adic groups, Mem. AMS 248 (2017) [25]; C. Perez-Garcia, W. H. Schikhof, Locally convex spaces over non-Archimedean valued fields [69]; O. Varol, On the derived tensor product functors for (DF)- and Fréchet spaces [82]; E. M. Mangino, (LF)-spaces and tensor products [56]; J. Wengenroth, Acyclic inductive spectra of Fréchet spaces [85]
prerequisites.why: The functional-analytic toolbox of §2: spaces of compact type and the LB property of a Hausdorff quotient (Emerton 1.1.17, 1.1.41), the coincidence of the projective and injective tensor topologies over a spherically complete field, the exactness of Hausdorff completion and the surjectivity of the last map in the Fréchet case, the interchange of the completed tensor product with regular nuclear inductive limits, and Wengenroth's criterion for acyclicity of an inductive spectrum.

prerequisites.citation: M. Boggi, G. Corob Cook, Continuous cohomology and homology of profinite groups, Doc. Math. 21 (2016) [9]; M. Witte, On a localisation sequence for the K-theory of skew power series rings, J. K-Theory 11 (2013) [86]; M. Kashiwara, P. Schapira, Ind-sheaves, Astérisque 271 (2001) [41]
prerequisites.why: The integral category the étale computation lives in: pro-discrete modules with their exactness properties, the presentation of a strict exact sequence as a limit of exact sequences of discrete modules (used to build the splitting in Lemma 2.7), the completed tensor product of pro-discrete modules with its universal property and right exactness on pseudocompact modules, and the quasi-abelianness of the ind-completion.

prerequisites.citation: V. Berkovich, Smooth p-adic analytic spaces are locally contractible, Invent. Math. 137 (1999), 1–84 [3]; Complex analytic vanishing cycles for formal schemes [4]; On the comparison theorem for étale cohomology of non-Archimedean analytic spaces, Israel J. Math. 92 (1995) [2]
prerequisites.why: That the log structure of a semistable formal scheme is canonical, so that M^gp(U) = O(U_K)^* and every Chern class map is a map out of the units of the generic fibre (his Theorem 5.3 and [4, Theorem 2.3.1]); and the comparison and vanishing statements quoted for rigid versus convergent cohomology of a proper smooth k-scheme and for the p-adic étale cohomology of rigid affine space.

prerequisites.citation: J. Fresnel, M. van der Put, Rigid analytic geometry and its applications, Progr. Math. 218 (2004) [27]; T. Saito, Weight spectral sequences and independence of ℓ, J. Inst. Math. Jussieu 2 (2003) [71]
prerequisites.why: The semistable models of the examples: Fresnel–van der Put's Theorem 4.9.1 builds a formal semistable model of P_K minus the limit set of an infinite compact set of rational points, which gives the models of rigid affine space and of the torus after modification to weak formal schemes, and Saito's Lemma 1.9 supplies the canonical ideal sheaf whose blow-up resolves the product model in dimension > 1.

prerequisites.citation: M. Gros, Classes de Chern et classes de cycles en cohomologie de Hodge–Witt logarithmique, Mém. SMF 21 (1985) [28]; E. de Shalit, The p-adic monodromy-weight conjecture for p-adically uniformized varieties, Compos. Math. 141 (2005) [22]
prerequisites.why: The de Rham–Witt Chern classes and their compatibility with the crystalline ones: de Shalit's 2.1 defines c^{log}_1 and c^{HK}_1 with logarithmic de Rham–Witt complexes, and Gros's I.5 gives the compatibility, with O^* replaced by M^gp in the logarithmic setting. These are the classes the integral regulator r_log integrates.

prerequisites.citation: S. Orlik, The de Rham cohomology of Drinfeld's half space, Münster J. Math. 8 (2015), 169–179 [66]; S. Orlik, B. Schraen, The Jordan–Hölder series of the locally analytic Steinberg representation, Doc. Math. 19 (2014), 647–671 [67]; A. Borel, N. Wallach, Continuous cohomology, discrete subgroups, and representations of reductive groups [10]; M.-F. Vignéras, Représentations ℓ-modulaires d'un groupe réductif p-adique [84]
prerequisites.why: The representation theory around the Steinberg representations: Casselman's theorem that the Sp_J are the irreducible constituents of LC(G/B,A) in characteristic 0 (Borel–Wallach X.4.11) with Vignéras's counterexample for ℓ ≠ p, Orlik's independent computation of the de Rham cohomology of the half-space and of its compactly supported analogue, and the Jordan–Hölder series of the locally analytic Steinberg representation quoted in Remark 5.5.

sourceIssues.printed: There is a natural G_K-equivariant map ι : B̂^+_st → B^+_dR induced by the maps p_ϖ : B̂^+_st → B^+_cr,K, B^+_cr/F^r ≅→ B^+_cr,K/F^r ≅← B^+_cr/F^r, where p_ϖ denotes the map induced by sending T ↦ ϖ. The composition B^+_st → B̂^+_st —ι→ B̂^+_dR is the map ι = ι_ϖ from Section 1.4.2.
sourceIssues.correction: … B^+_cr/F^r ≅→ B^+_cr,K/F^r ≅← B^+_dR/F^r …, and the composition B^+_st → B̂^+_st —ι→ B^+_dR.
sourceIssues.reason: Two slips in one sentence. The displayed chain has the same ring B^+_cr/F^r at both ends, so it produces no map to B^+_dR and the announced ι : B̂^+_st → B^+_dR is not defined; the third term must be B^+_dR/F^r, which is what the comparison of the graded pieces of A_cr and A_cr,K just quoted from Tsuji (Lemma 4.6.2) identifies with B^+_cr,K/F^r. And B̂^+_dR is defined nowhere in the paper: the target of ι_ϖ in §1.4.2 is B^+_dR. This map is used in the definition of RΓ_syn(X_C,Q_p(r)) and in every fundamental diagram.

review.reason: Rejected as a missing-hypothesis finding. The printed reference to §2.1.3 does not by itself justify the general interchange, but the asserted need to add regularity and nuclear transition maps is false. Use the Banach injective resolution already invoked in the proof. Over the complete discretely valued K, every closed subspace of a Banach space is complemented (Schneider, Nonarchimedean Functional Analysis, Proposition 10.5(a), proof read together with 10.1). Each short exact segment of that resolution therefore splits continuously. The additive completed tensor functor V⊗̂_K− preserves these splittings, giving a split exact tensor resolution without interchanging any inductive limit. Equivalently, the resulting contracting homotopy is preserved. This establishes the needed exactness in the paper’s setting without the proposed extra hypothesis on V. The general nonarchimedean injective-resolution construction remains an explicit supplier contract, not something formally supplied by the cited complex-analytic Prosmans paper. v2 has the same proof paragraph.

gaps.detail: Remark 1.7 observes that for small Tate twists (r ≤ p−1) the Fontaine–Messing period map is an isomorphism on the nose, so that with better control of the constants the proof would give the integral statement H^r_ét(H^d_C,F_p(r)) ≅ Sp_r(F_p)^*, and announces that, combined with the integral p-adic Hodge theory of Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze and Česnavičius–Koshikawa, such a result holds for all twists — but that is proved in the sequel [18] (PAPER-COLMEZ-DOSPINESCU-NIZIOL-21, 'Integral p-adic étale cohomology of Drinfeld symmetric spaces', job #1322), not here. Remark 6.46 likewise only announces the étale regulator r_ét of that sequel. Neither may be planned as a target of this paper's routes.

The paper states that the foundations of log-rigid cohomology are missing, so that RΓ_rig(Y/O^0_F) has to be constructed by hand following Grosse-Klönne (§3.1.2, p. 14, with a pointer to Shiho's relative log convergent cohomology as a partial substitute). A design job must therefore plan the hand-made construction — embedding systems, exactifications, tubes, the hocolim over hypercovers and the independence of choices — and not assume a general theory of log-rigid cohomology; the same applies to log-schemes with boundary, whose rigid cohomology is quoted from Grosse-Klönne's §1.10 under a mild condition that is only described there.

Remark 4.4 reviews relative convergent cohomology (enlargements, invariance under infinitesimal thickenings, the Poincaré lemma, the comparison with crystalline cohomology) from Ogus and Shiho, and Proposition 4.5 compares it with overconvergent rigid cohomology when the components of the special fibre are proper. Convergent cohomology is the subject of the Part II that PAPER-KISIN-MADAPUSIPERA-SHIN-22 proposes under CrystallineCohomology; that proposal is not yet an atlas stage, so the items are routed with this paper's machine and a design job should import them from that Part II once it exists rather than planning convergent cohomology twice.

The semistable weak formal models of rigid affine space and of the rigid torus used in §4.3 are obtained by modifying Fresnel–van der Put's Theorem 4.9.1 to weak formal schemes ('the proof is easily modified'), and in dimension > 1 by resolving the singularities of a product with the combinatorics of the monoids and a blow-up along the canonical ideal sheaf of Saito's Lemma 1.9. Neither modification is carried out in the paper, so a layer that needs these models must plan them.

The term pro-ordinary is used in the title of §6.2.4 and in the introduction ('the fact that X_k̄ is pro-ordinary, see Corollary 6.18') but is never defined; what is proved is that all the truncations Y_s, s ∈ N ∪ {∞}, are ordinary in the sense of Lemma 6.13. Corollary 6.18 is moreover deduced from 'Lemma 6.13 and Proposition 6.7', which only covers s < ∞: the case s = ∞ needs Proposition 6.5 for Y and the holim argument inside the proof of Lemma 6.20(3) for Ȳ. Remark 6.19 adds that the underlying scheme of Y_s is classically ordinary by the weight spectral sequence and that Corollary 6.18 'should be provable in an analogous way', which is not done.

Several statements in the paper are expectations rather than results: that Lemma A.1 (the splitting of Z^j_∞) 'holds most likely in much greater generality' than the semistable case proved here; that the alternative argument of Remark 6.19 for pro-ordinarity works; and that the map γ_HK of (6.36) can be identified in general — it is only for the Drinfeld half-space, where the sheaves of differentials are acyclic, that its source and target simplify enough to compute it. None of these may be planned as a target.

The map RΓ_syn(X,Z_p(r))_{Q_p} → RΓ_syn(X,Q_p(r)) between the integral and the sheafified rational Fontaine–Messing syntomic cohomology is a quasi-isomorphism for X of finite type 'but not in general' (§3.3.1, (3.44)), because the first inverts p only after taking global sections. This is why the pro-étale theorem is stated with Q_p(r)-coefficients and the étale theorem with Z_p(r)_{Q_p}, and why §6 has to redo integrally what §§3–4 do rationally; a design job must keep the two theories distinct.

All inherited 47 definition/construction records lack planningAPI and unitTests. Derive constructors, maps, functoriality, topology/base-change laws and positive/negative examples from their actual consumers; do not defer all contracts to design.

The inherited extraction had zero uses edges and 22 grouped prerequisite citations. This review adds only a source-checked partial dependency graph. Split, among others, Lemma 3.8/Proposition 3.9, Example 3.16/Lemma 3.20, all acyclicity results in 6-acyclicity-differentials, Propositions 6.9–6.12/Lemma 6.13, every part of Theorems 6.28/6.45, and Appendix Lemmas A.1/A.2. Read the original proofs of every quoted load-bearing result and route its definitions and intermediate lemmas exactly once.

Routes 1–9 and 11 are rejected proposals, preserved for stable identifiers. Resolve shared dagger geometry (AdicSpacesPartII F1), ordinary rigid cohomology (RD.3–5), log/HK scope (CR continuation), nonproper comparison (CP continuation), local representation theory (SR plus the Ding proposal), and generic topological derived foundations before creating design jobs. Existing paper proposals are not accepted atlas suppliers merely because their status says complete.

The public September 2019 manuscript is the checked source. Publisher preview and DOI metadata do not verify its identity with the journal version of record. The Illusie 1990 original Proposition 1.6 was not acquired in this review; E32 is established by a direct Cartier-divisor counterexample, not an asserted reading of that proposition. The full nonarchimedean adaptation of Prosmans remains a supplier proof task.

changes.from: Let r ≥ 0; for i > 0 the spaces H^i_ét(Ȳ,WΩ^r) and H^i_ét(Ȳ,WΩ^r_log) vanish, and in degree 0 there are natural isomorphisms of locally convex Q_p-vector spaces — more precisely of weak duals of Banach spaces — H^0(Ȳ,WΩ^r) ⊗_{O_F} F ≅ H^r(Ȳ,WΩ^•) ⊗_{O_F} F ≅ Sp^cont_r(F)^*, H^0_ét(Y,WΩ^r_log) ⊗ Q_p ≅ Sp^cont_r(Q_p)^*, H^0(X,Ω^r) ⊗_{O_K} K ≅ H^r_dR(X) ⊗_{O_K} K ≅ Sp^cont_r(K)^*, and H^0_ét(Ȳ,WΩ^r_log) ⊗ Q_p ≅ Sp^cont_r(Q_p)^*; and integrally, natural isomorphisms of pro-discrete Z_p-modules H^0_ét(Ȳ,WΩ^r) ≅ H^r_ét(Ȳ,WΩ^•) ≅ Sp^cont_r(O_F)^*, H^0(Ȳ,Ω^r) ≅ Sp_r(k̄)^*, H^0_ét(Y,WΩ^r_log) ≅ Sp^cont_r(Z_p)^*, H^0_ét(Y,Ω^r_log) ≅ Sp_r(F_p)^*, H^0(X,Ω^r) ≅ H^r_dR(X) ≅ Sp^cont_r(O_K)^*, all compatible with the canonical maps between Steinberg representations and with the isomorphisms H^r_dR(X_K) ≅ Sp_r(K)^* and H^r_HK(X) ≅ Sp_r(F)^* of Theorem 5.10 and Lemma 5.11.
changes.to: Let K/Q_p be finite, X the standard formal model of H^d_K, Y=X_0 and Ȳ=Y_{k̄}. changes.from: Three continuous regulators are defined by integrating the Chern classes of the Appendix: r_HK out of D(H^{r+1},O_F) using the crystalline Hyodo–Kato classes c^{HK}_1, r_log out of D(H^{r+1},Z_p) using the crystalline logarithmic de Rham–Witt classes c^{log}_1, and r_dR out of D(H^{r+1},O_K) using the integral de Rham classes c^{dR}_1. In each case a diagram — combining the canonical surjection onto the continuous Steinberg dual, the injection ι_Y of Proposition 6.27, Lemma 5.11 and §7.2.1 — produces a broken arrow Sp^cont_r(O_F)^* → H^0_ét(Ȳ,WΩ^r), continuous and injective, whose composite with ι_Y is the canonical embedding into Sp_r(F)^*; since H^0_ét(Ȳ,WΩ^r) is compact its image lies in the G-bounded vectors, identified with Sp^cont_r(F)^*, so H^0_ét(Ȳ,WΩ^r) is a G-equivariant lattice in Sp^cont_r(F)^* and hence homothetic to Sp^cont_r(O_F)^* by Corollary 5.3; modulo p the target H^0_ét(Ȳ,Ω^r) ≅ Sp_r(k̄)^* is irreducible and the reduced regulator is non-zero because the symbol dlog z_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ dlog z_r is in its image. The logarithmic diagram shows in addition that f : H^r_ét(Ȳ,WΩ^•_log) ↪ H^r_ét(Ȳ,WΩ^•)^{φ=p^r} and r_log are isomorphisms.
changes.to: For K/Q_p finite and the standard model X with Y=X_0, define the continuous regulators r_HK from D(H^{r+1},O_F), r_log from D(H^{r+1},Z_p), and r_dR from D(H^{r+1},O_K) by integrating the corresponding first Chern classes of §7 and their cup products. Diagrams (6.29)–(6.31) factor them through the continuous Steinberg duals. In the Hyodo–Kato diagram the resulting map Sp^cont_r(O_F)^* → H^0_ét(Y,WΩ^r) is continuous and injective and its rational composite is the canonical inclusion into Sp_r(F)^*. The target is compact over O_F because k is finite; bounded vectors, Corollary 5.3 and the nonzero mod-p symbol give the integral isomorphism, whose reduction is over k, not k̄. changes.to: Projective spaces are ordinary, and projective bundles over an ordinary base are ordinary. For a smooth closed centre Y of codimension at least two in proper smooth X, the usual blow-up criterion says X and Y are ordinary if and only if Bl_Y(X) is; the paper omits that codimension qualification (source issue E32). changes.from: Relative convergent cohomology is well developed (Ogus, Shiho): its site is defined like the crystalline one with PD-thickenings replaced by enlargements — p-adic formal schemes, analytically closed discs of any radius < 1 rather than of a fixed radius — and convergent cohomology is the cohomology of the rational structure sheaf on it. It is invariant under homeomorphic exact closed immersions; a Poincaré lemma computes it locally by de Rham complexes of convergent tubes of log-smooth formal log-schemes, with open discs replacing the fixed closed discs of the crystalline theory; and the natural map to crystalline cohomology is a quasi-isomorphism for log-schemes log-smooth over the reduction of the base, so RΓ_conv(X_0/O^0_F) ≅ RΓ_cr(X_0/O^0_{F,F}) for X_0 semistable. Proposition 4.5 (Grosse-Klönne, Theorem 5.3): if all irreducible components of X_0 are proper then RΓ_rig(X_0/O^0_F) → RΓ_conv(X_0/O^0_F) is a quasi-isomorphism, by comparing the two weight spectral sequences and the classical statement H^*_rig(S/O_F) ≅ H^*_conv(S/O_F) for S smooth and proper over k.

changes.from: Let J = ker(p_0 : r^PD_ϖ → O_F, T ↦ 0), a Frobenius- and monodromy-compatible map. From 0 → J_n → r^PD_{ϖ,n} → O_{F,n} → 0, tensoring with the flat Â_st,n and passing to the limit gives 0 → E → Â_st —p_0→ O_F ⊗̂_{r^PD_ϖ} Â_st → 0 with E := J ⊗̂_{r^PD_ϖ} Â_st. changes.to: For a map between topological spaces, Topology.IsStrictMap f means IsQuotientMap of its range factorization. For linear maps between the stated topological modules, Mathlib identifies this with an open quotient onto the range and with a homeomorphism M/ker(f) ≃ range(f). This does not construct the paper’s exact category.

Let A be a commutative topological Tate ring. Let M,N be complete uniform additive groups with countably generated uniformities, A-modules, M nonarchimedean with continuous scalar action, and N T0 with continuous constant scalar multiplication. A linear map f:M→N continuous at zero is open and a quotient map if surjective; if its range is closed it is strict. These are the exact Tau Ceti implications; the LF theorem and the paper’s exact-category construction are separate.
